Sets and indices:
- T: set of trains, indexed by i (and j for a second train).
- R_i: ordered set of route sections (track sections / TDS) of train i, indexed by r; r=1..|R_i|. The route includes the section where the train is located at the start of the rescheduling horizon.
- S_i = {(r,s)}: set of candidate speed profile options for train i on route section r, indexed by s in 1..n_{i,r}. Each speed profile option s for train i on section r is defined by an entry speed v^in_{i,r,s} and a (speed-dependent) traversal time.
- C: set of conflicting pairs (i,r,j,r') meaning that section r of train i and section r' of train j correspond to the same physical track resource (block section / TTD section) and the trains may conflict. This includes pairs of trains with common route sections.
- SW: subset of sections that are switches (turnouts); other sections are open line or platform track sections.

Parameters:
- t^0_{i,r}: scheduled (planned) arrival time of train i at the entry of section r from the original timetable.
- d^0_i: entrance delay of train i at the start of the horizon (delay at its first section).
- l_{i,r,s}: minimum running (traversal) time of train i on section r under speed profile s (depends on entry speed and section length, speed-dependent under DTG).
- f_i: scheduled dwell time of train i at the station located on its route (if any; otherwise 0); dwell is performed on a designated section.
- B_{i,r,s}(v): braking distance of train i when braking from speed v under profile s on section r. Under DTG/ETCS L2 the separation between two consecutive trains on the same track depends on the absolute braking distance of the following train: the following train must receive its movement authority (MA) such that its supervised braking curve ends at the end of authority (EoA) located at the end of the last free block section/TDS before the preceding train. The brake indication point can lie anywhere along the track and is speed-dependent.
- o_{i,r,j,r',s}: minimum separation (blocking) time headway required between train i occupying section r with speed profile s and the following train j entering the corresponding conflicting section r', computed from the speed-dependent braking distance B and the approach speed (train- and speed-dependent blocking time). For conventional fixed-block this would be a constant number of block traversals; here it varies with s.
- a_{i,r}: 1 if section r of train i is a switch (in SW), 0 otherwise.
- M: a sufficiently large constant (big-M).
- w_i: weight/priority of train i in the objective (assumption: equals 1 for all trains if not specified).
- delta: maximum allowed deviation from the scheduled arrival times (assumption, to bound the horizon).

Decision variables:
- t_{i,r} >= 0: continuous variable, arrival (entry) time of train i at section r (rescheduled).
- x_{i,r,s} in {0,1}: binary variable, 1 if train i traverses section r with speed profile s.
- y_{i,r,j,r'} in {0,1}: binary sequencing variable for each conflicting pair (i,r,j,r'), 1 if train i enters the shared resource before train j, 0 otherwise (disjunctive ordering variable).

Objective function:
Minimise the total weighted train delay at a relevant reference point (e.g., at the exit of the rescheduling horizon or at scheduled stops). For each train i, the delay is measured at the last section of its route: D_i = max(0, t_{i,last} - t^0_{i,last}). Since this is linear via t_{i,last} >= t^0_{i,last} when delays are nonnegative after optimisation, minimise sum_i w_i * (t_{i,|R_i|} - t^0_{i,|R_i|}). Alternatively use deviation variables e_i >= t_{i,|R_i|} - t^0_{i,|R_i|}, e_i >= 0 and minimise sum_i w_i e_i.

Constraints:
1. Speed profile selection: for each train i and each section r on its route, exactly one speed profile is chosen: sum_s x_{i,r,s} = 1.
2.    t_{i,r} >= t_{j,r'} + sum_s o_{j,r',i,r,s'} x_{j,r',s'} - M y_{i,r,j,r'}

Hence for (i,r,j,r') with r (or r') in SW use o^{SW}_{i,r,j,r',s} >= o_{i,r,j,r',s} (larger headway), and possibly additional pairwise constraints between the section preceding the switch and the switch section itself to model route locking before the train reaches the switch (assumption).

Mark as optional/assumption.
8. Variable domains: t_{i,r} >= 0 (or >= lower bounds), x binary, y binary.

# Railway Conflict Detection and Resolution MILP Implementation

Below is a complete Python implementation using PuLP (which works with free solvers like CBC) with a Gurobi alternative. The model extends RECIFE-MILP with ETCS Level 2 DTG signalling features.

```python
"""
Railway Conflict Detection and Resolution (CDR) MILP
Extending RECIFE-MILP (Pellegrini et al., 2015) with:
- ETCS Level 2 Distance-To-Go (DTG) signalling
- Train- and speed-dependent braking distances
- Multiple speed profiles per train per section
- Switch-specific blocking constraints

Author: Generated implementation
"""

import pulp
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple, Optional, Set
import itertools


# =============================================================================
# DATA STRUCTURES FOR MODEL PARAMETERS
# =============================================================================

@dataclass
class SpeedProfile:
    """Speed profile option for a train on a section."""
    entry_speed: float          # v^in: entry speed (km/h or m/s)
    exit_speed: float           # v^out: exit speed
    traversal_time: float       # l: minimum running time (seconds)
    braking_distance: float     # B(v): braking distance from entry speed (meters)


@dataclass
class Section:
    """Route section (track section / TDS)."""
    section_id: int             # Physical section identifier
    is_switch: bool             # a_{i,r}: True if switch/turnout
    is_stop: bool               # True if scheduled stop (station)
    dwell_time: float = 0.0     # f_i: scheduled dwell time (seconds)
    speed_profiles: List[SpeedProfile] = field(default_factory=list)


@dataclass
class Train:
    """Train with its route and timetable."""
    train_id: str
    route: List[Section]                    # Ordered list of sections
    scheduled_times: List[float]            # t^0_{i,r}: scheduled arrival times
    entrance_delay: float = 0.0             # d^0_i: delay at start of horizon
    weight: float = 1.0                     # w_i: priority weight


@dataclass
class ConflictPair:
    """Conflicting pair of train-section combinations."""
    train_i: str
    section_idx_i: int          # Index in train_i's route
    train_j: str
    section_idx_j: int          # Index in train_j's route
    physical_resource: int      # Common physical section ID
    # Headway matrix: o[i][j][s] = separation time for train i with profile s
    # followed by train j
    headways_ij: Dict[int, float] = field(default_factory=dict)  # Keyed by profile index of train i
    headways_ji: Dict[int, float] = field(default_factory=dict)  # Keyed by profile index of train j


# =============================================================================
# EXAMPLE DATA GENERATION (Replace with actual infrastructure data)
# =============================================================================

def create_example_data():
    """
    Create example railway network data.
    In practice, this would be loaded from infrastructure database and timetable.
    """
    
    # Define physical sections
    # Section IDs: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (where 3 is a switch)
    
    # Speed profiles for different sections
    # Profile 0: Low speed approach (e.g., 60 km/h)
    # Profile 1: Medium speed (e.g., 100 km/h)
    # Profile 2: High speed (e.g., 160 km/h)
    
    def make_profiles(base_time: float, length: float):
        """Create speed profiles with varying speeds and times."""
        profiles = []
        speeds = [(60, 55), (100, 95), (160, 155)]  # (entry, exit) km/h
        for idx, (v_in, v_out) in enumerate(speeds):
            # Simplified: traversal time inversely proportional to average speed
            avg_speed = (v_in + v_out) / 2
            time = base_time * (100 / avg_speed)  # Normalize to 100 km/h baseline
            # Braking distance: simplified model d = v^2 / (2*a), a = 0.8 m/s^2
            v_ms = v_in / 3.6  # Convert to m/s
            braking_dist = (v_ms ** 2) / (2 * 0.8)
            profiles.append(SpeedProfile(
                entry_speed=v_in,
                exit_speed=v_out,
                traversal_time=time,
                braking_distance=braking_dist
            ))
        return profiles
    
    # Create sections for Train 1 (route: 1 -> 3 -> 4)
    sections_t1 = [
        Section(1, is_switch=False, is_stop=False, speed_profiles=make_profiles(60, 1000)),
        Section(3, is_switch=True, is_stop=False, speed_profiles=make_profiles(45, 500)),
        Section(4, is_switch=False, is_stop=True, dwell_time=120, speed_profiles=make_profiles(80, 800)),
    ]
    
    # Create sections for Train 2 (route: 2 -> 3 -> 5)
    sections_t2 = [
        Section(2, is_switch=False, is_stop=False, speed_profiles=make_profiles(70, 1200)),
        Section(3, is_switch=True, is_stop=False, speed_profiles=make_profiles(40, 500)),
        Section(5, is_switch=False, is_stop=False, speed_profiles=make_profiles(90, 900)),
    ]
    
    # Create sections for Train 3 (route: 4 -> 3 -> 2) - reverse direction
    sections_t3 = [
        Section(4, is_switch=False, is_stop=True, dwell_time=120, speed_profiles=make_profiles(75, 800)),
        Section(3, is_switch=True, is_stop=False, speed_profiles=make_profiles(50, 500)),
        Section(2, is_switch=False, is_stop=False, speed_profiles=make_profiles(85, 1200)),
    ]
    
    # Create trains with scheduled times (seconds from horizon start)
    trains = {
        'T1': Train(
            train_id='T1',
            route=sections_t1,
            scheduled_times=[0, 60, 200],  # Arrival at sections 1, 3, 4
            entrance_delay=30,              # 30 seconds late at entrance
            weight=1.0
        ),
        'T2': Train(
            train_id='T2',
            route=sections_t2,
            scheduled_times=[10, 80, 220],  # Arrival at sections 2, 3, 5
            entrance_delay=0,
            weight=1.0
        ),
        'T3': Train(
            train_id='T3',
            route=sections_t3,
            scheduled_times=[100, 180, 280],  # Arrival at sections 4, 3, 2
            entrance_delay=0,
            weight=1.0
        ),
    }
    
    # Create conflict pairs
    # Conflicts occur where trains share physical sections
    conflicts = []
    
    # Helper to compute headway based on braking distance
    def compute_headway(braking_dist: float, speed_kmh: float, is_switch: bool = False) -> float:
        """
        Compute separation headway under ETCS L2 DTG.
        Following train must be able to brake to EoA at end of last free TDS.
        """
        v_ms = speed_kmh / 3.6
        # Time to traverse braking distance at constant deceleration + safety margin
        brake_time = 2 * braking_dist / v_ms if v_ms > 0 else 0
        safety_margin = 5.0  # seconds
        switch_penalty = 20.0 if is_switch else 0.0  # Additional time for switch locking
        return brake_time + safety_margin + switch_penalty
    
    # Find all pairs of trains with common sections
    train_list = list(trains.values())
    for i, t1 in enumerate(train_list):
        for j, t2 in enumerate(train_list):
            if i >= j:
                continue
            # Find common physical sections
            for r1_idx, s1 in enumerate(t1.route):
                for r2_idx, s2 in enumerate(t2.route):
                    if s1.section_id == s2.section_id:
                        # Create conflict pair
                        is_switch = s1.is_switch
                        cp = ConflictPair(
                            train_i=t1.train_id,
                            section_idx_i=r1_idx,
                            train_j=t2.train_id,
                            section_idx_j=r2_idx,
                            physical_resource=s1.section_id,
                            headways_ij={},
                            headways_ji={}
                        )
                        # Compute headways for each speed profile combination
                        for s_idx, prof in enumerate(s1.speed_profiles):
                            cp.headways_ij[s_idx] = compute_headway(
                                prof.braking_distance, prof.entry_speed, is_switch
                            )
                        for s_idx, prof in enumerate(s2.speed_profiles):
                            cp.headways_ji[s_idx] = compute_headway(
                                prof.braking_distance, prof.entry_speed, is_switch
                            )
                        conflicts.append(cp)
    
    # Parameters
    M = 10000  # Big-M constant (should be larger than max possible delay)
    delta = 3600  # Maximum deviation from schedule (1 hour)
    
    return trains, conflicts, M, delta


# =============================================================================
# MILP MODEL FORMULATION
# =============================================================================

class RailwayCDRModel:
    """
    Mixed-Integer Linear Programming model for railway conflict resolution.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, trains: Dict[str, Train], conflicts: List[ConflictPair],
                 M: float = 10000, delta: float = 3600):
        self.trains = trains
        self.conflicts = conflicts
        self.M = M
        self.delta = delta
        self.model = None
        self.t = {}  # Arrival time variables
        self.x = {}  # Speed profile selection variables
        self.y = {}  # Sequencing variables
        self.e = {}  # Delay deviation variables
        
    def build_model(self):
        """Construct the MILP model."""
        
        # Create model
        self.model = pulp.LpProblem("Railway_CDR", pulp.LpMinimize)
        
        # =====================================================================
        # DECISION VARIABLES
        # =====================================================================
        
        # t_{i,r}: arrival time of train i at section r
        for train_id, train in self.trains.items():
            for r in range(len(train.route)):
                lb = train.scheduled_times[r] + (train.entrance_delay if r == 0 else 0)
                ub = train.scheduled_times[r] + self.delta
                self.t[(train_id, r)] = pulp.LpVariable(
                    f"t_{train_id}_{r}", lowBound=lb, upBound=ub
                )
        
        # x_{i,r,s}: binary, 1 if train i uses speed profile s on section r
        for train_id, train in self.trains.items():
            for r, section in enumerate(train.route):
                for s in range(len(section.speed_profiles)):
                    self.x[(train_id, r, s)] = pulp.LpVariable(
                        f"x_{train_id}_{r}_{s}", cat='Binary'
                    )
        
        # y_{i,j,r,r'}: binary sequencing variable for conflicts
        # Use canonical ordering (i < j) to avoid duplicate variables
        for cp in self.conflicts:
            key = (cp.train_i, cp.train_j, cp.section_idx_i, cp.section_idx_j)
            self.y[key] = pulp.LpVariable(
                f"y_{cp.train_i}_{cp.train_j}_{cp.section_idx_i}_{cp.section_idx_j}",
                cat='Binary'
            )
        
        # e_i: delay deviation variable for objective
        for train_id, train in self.trains.items():
            self.e[train_id] = pulp.LpVariable(f"e_{train_id}", lowBound=0)
        
        # =====================================================================
        # OBJECTIVE FUNCTION
        # Minimize total weighted delay at exit of rescheduling horizon
        # =====================================================================
        
        objective = pulp.lpSum([
            train.weight * self.e[train_id]
            for train_id, train in self.trains.items()
        ])
        self.model += objective, "Total_Weighted_Delay"
        
        # =====================================================================
        # CONSTRAINTS
        # =====================================================================
        
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Constraint 1: Speed profile selection
        # Exactly one speed profile per train per section
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        for train_id, train in self.trains.items():
            for r, section in enumerate(train.route):
                n_profiles = len(section.speed_profiles)
                self.model += (
                    pulp.lpSum([self.x[(train_id, r, s)] for s in range(n_profiles)]) == 1,
                    f"ProfileSelect_{train_id}_{r}"
                )
        
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Constraint 2: Running time / precedence along route
        # t_{i,r+1} >= t_{i,r} + sum_s l_{i,r,s} * x_{i,r,s} + f_{i,r}
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        for train_id, train in self.trains.items():
            for r in range(len(train.route) - 1):
                section = train.route[r]
                n_profiles = len(section.speed_profiles)
                
                # Running time expression
                running_time = pulp.lpSum([
                    section.speed_profiles[s].traversal_time * self.x[(train_id, r, s)]
                    for s in range(n_profiles)
                ])
                
                # Add dwell time if this is a stop
                dwell = section.dwell_time if section.is_stop else 0
                
                self.model += (
                    self.t[(train_id, r + 1)] >= self.t[(train_id, r)] + running_time + dwell,
                    f"RunningTime_{train_id}_{r}"
                )
        
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Constraint 3: Scheduled lower bounds / no early departure
        # t_{i,r} >= t^0_{i,r} for scheduled stops and first section
        # Also: t_{i,1} >= d^0_i + t^0_{i,1} (entrance delay)
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        for train_id, train in self.trains.items():
            for r, section in enumerate(train.route):
                scheduled_time = train.scheduled_times[r]
                
                # First section: include entrance delay
                if r == 0:
                    lb = scheduled_time + train.entrance_delay
                    self.model += (
                        self.t[(train_id, r)] >= lb,
                        f"EntranceDelay_{train_id}_{r}"
                    )
                
                # Scheduled stops: no early departure
                if section.is_stop or r == 0:
                    self.model += (
                        self.t[(train_id, r)] >= scheduled_time,
                        f"NoEarly_{train_id}_{r}"
                    )
        
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Constraint 5: Conflict (disjunctive) constraints
        # For each conflicting pair, ensure separation with speed-dependent headway
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        for cp in self.conflicts:
            train_i = self.trains[cp.train_i]
            train_j = self.trains[cp.train_j]
            section_i = train_i.route[cp.section_idx_i]
            section_j = train_j.route[cp.section_idx_j]
            
            key = (cp.train_i, cp.train_j, cp.section_idx_i, cp.section_idx_j)
            y_var = self.y[key]
            
            # Headway for train i with each profile
            n_profiles_i = len(section_i.speed_profiles)
            headway_i = pulp.lpSum([
                cp.headways_ij.get(s, 30) * self.x[(cp.train_i, cp.section_idx_i, s)]
                for s in range(n_profiles_i)
            ])
            
            # Headway for train j with each profile
            n_profiles_j = len(section_j.speed_profiles)
            headway_j = pulp.lpSum([
                cp.headways_ji.get(s, 30) * self.x[(cp.train_j, cp.section_idx_j, s)]
                for s in range(n_profiles_j)
            ])
            
            # Disjunctive constraints:
            # If y = 1: train i goes before train j
            # t_j >= t_i + headway_i - M*(1-y)
            self.model += (
                self.t[(cp.train_j, cp.section_idx_j)] >= 
                self.t[(cp.train_i, cp.section_idx_i)] + headway_i - self.M * (1 - y_var),
                f"Conflict_ij_{cp.train_i}_{cp.train_j}_{cp.section_idx_i}_{cp.section_idx_j}"
            )
            
            # If y = 0: train j goes before train i
            # t_i >= t_j + headway_j - M*y
            self.model += (
                self.t[(cp.train_i, cp.section_idx_i)] >= 
                self.t[(cp.train_j, cp.section_idx_j)] + headway_j - self.M * y_var,
                f"Conflict_ji_{cp.train_i}_{cp.train_j}_{cp.section_idx_i}_{cp.section_idx_j}"
            )
        
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Constraint 6: Switch-specific constraints
        # Additional constraints for switch route locking
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        for cp in self.conflicts:
            train_i = self.trains[cp.train_i]
            train_j = self.trains[cp.train_j]
            section_i = train_i.route[cp.section_idx_i]
            section_j = train_j.route[cp.section_idx_j]
            
            # If either section is a switch, add extended blocking constraints
            if section_i.is_switch or section_j.is_switch:
                # For switches: block the resource from entry until clear
                # This is modeled by extending the headway (already done in data)
                # Additional constraint: route locking before switch entry
                
                # If there's a preceding section, ensure it's also blocked
                if cp.section_idx_i > 0 and section_i.is_switch:
                    # The approach section must also be clear before entering switch
                    pass  # Handled implicitly through running time constraints
                
                # Switch release time: train must clear switch before other can enter
                # This is captured in the increased headway for switches
                pass
        
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Constraint 7: Speed consistency across consecutive sections (optional)
        # Exit speed of section r should approximately equal entry speed of r+1
        # Linearized using binary variables
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        for train_id, train in self.trains.items():
            for r in range(len(train.route) - 1):
                section_curr = train.route[r]
                section_next = train.route[r + 1]
                
                # Get exit speeds for current section profiles
                n_curr = len(section_curr.speed_profiles)
                n_next = len(section_next.speed_profiles)
                
                # For each profile combination, check speed compatibility
                # Add constraint: if x_curr[s1] = 1 and x_next[s2] = 1, 
                # then |v_out[s1] - v_in[s2]| <= tolerance
                tolerance = 20  # km/h tolerance for speed continuity
                
                for s1 in range(n_curr):
                    v_out = section_curr.speed_profiles[s1].exit_speed
                    for s2 in range(n_next):
                        v_in = section_next.speed_profiles[s2].entry_speed
                        
                        if abs(v_out - v_in) > tolerance:
                            # Incompatible: x[s1] + x[s2] <= 1
                            self.model += (
                                self.x[(train_id, r, s1)] + self.x[(train_id, r + 1, s2)] <= 1,
                                f"SpeedCompat_{train_id}_{r}_{s1}_{s2}"
                            )
        
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        # Delay deviation constraint for objective
        # e_i >= t_{i,last} - t^0_{i,last}
        # e_i >= 0 (already in variable bounds)
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        for train_id, train in self.trains.items():
            last_r = len(train.route) - 1
            scheduled_last = train.scheduled_times[last_r]
            
            self.model += (
                self.e[train_id] >= self.t[(train_id, last_r)] - scheduled_last,
                f"DelayDev_{train_id}"
            )
        
        return self.model
    
    def solve(self, solver=None, time_limit: int = 300, gap: float = 0.01):
        """
        Solve the MILP model.
        
        Args:
            solver: PuLP solver (default: CBC)
            time_limit: Maximum solve time in seconds
            gap: MIP optimality gap tolerance
        """
        if self.model is None:
            self.build_model()
        
        if solver is None:
            # Use CBC (free) or Gurobi if available
            try:
                solver = pulp.GUROBI_CMD(timeLimit=time_limit, options=[('MIPGap', gap)])
            except:
                solver = pulp.PULP_CBC_CMD(timeLimit=time_limit, gapRel=gap)
        
        self.model.solve(solver)
        
        return pulp.LpStatus[self.model.status]
    
    def get_solution(self) -> Dict:
        """Extract and return the solution."""
        if self.model is None or self.model.status != pulp.LpStatusOptimal:
            return {"status": pulp.LpStatus.get(self.model.status, "Not solved")}
        
        solution = {
            "status": "Optimal",
            "objective": pulp.value(self.model.objective),
            "trains": {},
            "conflicts": {}
        }
        
        # Extract train schedules
        for train_id, train in self.trains.items():
            schedule = []
            profiles = []
            for r in range(len(train.route)):
                t_val = pulp.value(self.t[(train_id, r)])
                scheduled = train.scheduled_times[r]
                delay = max(0, t_val - scheduled) if t_val else 0
                
                # Find selected profile
                selected_profile = None
                for s in range(len(train.route[r].speed_profiles)):
                    if pulp.value(self.x[(train_id, r, s)]) > 0.5:
                        selected_profile = s
                        break
                
                schedule.append({
                    "section_idx": r,
                    "section_id": train.route[r].section_id,
                    "arrival_time": t_val,
                    "scheduled_time": scheduled,
                    "delay": delay,
                    "is_switch": train.route[r].is_switch,
                    "is_stop": train.route[r].is_stop
                })
                profiles.append(selected_profile)
            
            solution["trains"][train_id] = {
                "schedule": schedule,
                "selected_profiles": profiles,
                "total_delay": pulp.value(self.e[train_id])
            }
        
        # Extract sequencing decisions
        for key, y_var in self.y.items():
            train_i, train_j, r_i, r_j = key
            y_val = pulp.value(y_var)
            solution["conflicts"][f"{train_i}_{r_i}_vs_{train_j}_{r_j}"] = {
                "order": f"{train_i} first" if y_val > 0.5 else f"{train_j} first",
                "y_value": y_val
            }
        
        return solution
    
    def print_solution(self):
        """Print formatted solution."""
        sol = self.get_solution()
        
        print("=" * 70)
        print("RAILWAY CONFLICT DETECTION AND RESOLUTION - SOLUTION")
        print("=" * 70)
        print(f"\nStatus: {sol['status']}")
        print(f"Total Weighted Delay: {sol.get('objective', 'N/A'):.2f} seconds")
        
        print("\n" + "-" * 70)
        print("TRAIN SCHEDULES")
        print("-" * 70)
        
        for train_id, data in sol.get("trains", {}).items():
            print(f"\nTrain {train_id} (Total delay: {data['total_delay']:.1f}s)")
            print(f"  Selected profiles: {data['selected_profiles']}")
            print(f"  {'Section':<10} {'Type':<12} {'Scheduled':<12} {'Actual':<12} {'Delay':<10}")
            print(f"  {'-'*56}")
            
            for entry in data["schedule"]:
                sec_type = []
                if entry["is_switch"]:
                    sec_type.append("SWITCH")
                if entry["is_stop"]:
                    sec_type.append("STOP")
                type_str = "/".join(sec_type) if sec_type else "LINE"
                
                print(f"  {entry['section_id']:<10} {type_str:<12} "
                      f"{entry['scheduled_time']:<12.1f} {entry['arrival_time']:<12.1f} "
                      f"{entry['delay']:<10.1f}")
        
        print("\n" + "-" * 70)
        print("CONFLICT RESOLUTIONS")
        print("-" * 70)
        for conflict, resolution in sol.get("conflicts", {}).items():
            print(f"  {conflict}: {resolution['order']}")
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)


# =============================================================================
# GUROBI ALTERNATIVE IMPLEMENTATION (More efficient for large problems)
# =============================================================================

def build_gurobi_model(trains: Dict[str, Train], conflicts: List[ConflictPair],
                       M: float = 10000, delta: float = 3600):
    """
    Build the MILP model using Gurobi directly (more efficient API).
    Requires: pip install gurobipy
    """
    try:
        import gurobipy as gp
        from gurobipy import GRB
    except ImportError:
        print("Gurobi not available. Install with: pip install gurobipy")
        return None
    
    model = gp.Model("Railway_CDR")
    
    # Decision variables
    t = {}  # Arrival times
    x = {}  # Speed profile selection
    y = {}  # Sequencing
    e = {}  # Delay deviation
    
    # Create variables
    for train_id, train in trains.items():
        for r in range(len(train.route)):
            lb = train.scheduled_times[r] + (train.entrance_delay if r == 0 else 0)
            ub = train.scheduled_times[r] + delta
            t[train_id, r] = model.addVar(lb=lb, ub=ub, name=f"t_{train_id}_{r}")
            
            for s in range(len(train.route[r].speed_profiles)):
                x[train_id, r, s] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"x_{train_id}_{r}_{s}")
        
        e[train_id] = model.addVar(lb=0, name=f"e_{train_id}")
    
    for cp in conflicts:
        key = (cp.train_i, cp.train_j, cp.section_idx_i, cp.section_idx_j)
        y[key] = model.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"y_{cp.train_i}_{cp.train_j}")
    
    # Objective: minimize total weighted delay
    model.setObjective(
        gp.quicksum(trains[tid].weight * e[tid] for tid in trains),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )
    
    # Constraint 1: Profile selection
    for train_id, train in trains.items():
        for r, section in enumerate(train.route):
            model.addConstr(
                gp.quicksum(x[train_id, r, s] for s in range(len(section.speed_profiles))) == 1,
                f"profile_{train_id}_{r}"
            )
    
    # Constraint 2: Running times
    for train_id, train in trains.items():
        for r in range(len(train.route) - 1):
            section = train.route[r]
            running = gp.quicksum(
                section.speed_profiles[s].traversal_time * x[train_id, r, s]
                for s in range(len(section.speed_profiles))
            )
            dwell = section.dwell_time if section.is_stop else 0
            model.addConstr(
                t[train_id, r+1] >= t[train_id, r] + running + dwell,
                f"running_{train_id}_{r}"
            )
    
    # Constraint 3: Lower bounds
    for train_id, train in trains.items():
        for r, section in enumerate(train.route):
            scheduled = train.scheduled_times[r]
            if r == 0:
                model.addConstr(
                    t[train_id, r] >= scheduled + train.entrance_delay,
                    f"entrance_{train_id}"
                )
            if section.is_stop or r == 0:
                model.addConstr(
                    t[train_id, r] >= scheduled,
                    f"noearly_{train_id}_{r}"
                )
    
    # Constraint 5: Conflicts
    for cp in conflicts:
        key = (cp.train_i, cp.train_j, cp.section_idx_i, cp.section_idx_j)
        y_var = y[key]
        
        train_i = trains[cp.train_i]
        train_j = trains[cp.train_j]
        section_i = train_i.route[cp.section_idx_i]
        section_j = train_j.route[cp.section_idx_j]
        
        headway_i = gp.quicksum(
            cp.headways_ij.get(s, 30) * x[cp.train_i, cp.section_idx_i, s]
            for s in range(len(section_i.speed_profiles))
        )
        headway_j = gp.quicksum(
            cp.headways_ji.get(s, 30) * x[cp.train_j, cp.section_idx_j, s]
            for s in range(len(section_j.speed_profiles))
        )
        
        model.addConstr(
            t[cp.train_j, cp.section_idx_j] >= 
            t[cp.train_i, cp.section_idx_i] + headway_i - M * (1 - y_var),
            f"conflict_ij_{key}"
        )
        model.addConstr(
            t[cp.train_i, cp.section_idx_i] >= 
            t[cp.train_j, cp.section_idx_j] + headway_j - M * y_var,
            f"conflict_ji_{key}"
        )
    
    # Speed consistency
    tolerance = 20
    for train_id, train in trains.items():
        for r in range(len(train.route) - 1):
            sec_curr = train.route[r]
            sec_next = train.route[r + 1]
            for s1 in range(len(sec_curr.speed_profiles)):
                v_out = sec_curr.speed_profiles[s1].exit_speed
                for s2 in range(len(sec_next.speed_profiles)):
                    v_in = sec_next.speed_profiles[s2].entry_speed
                    if abs(v_out - v_in) > tolerance:
                        model.addConstr(
                            x[train_id, r, s1] + x[train_id, r+1, s2] <= 1,
                            f"speed_{train_id}_{r}_{s1}_{s2}"
                        )
    
    # Delay deviation
    for train_id, train in trains.items():
        last_r = len(train.route) - 1
        model.addConstr(
            e[train_id] >= t[train_id, last_r] - train.scheduled_times[last_r],
            f"delay_{train_id}"
        )
    
    return model, {'t': t, 'x': x, 'y': y, 'e': e}


# =============================================================================
# MAIN EXECUTION
# =============================================================================

def main():
    """Main function to demonstrate the model."""
    
    print("Creating example railway network data...")
    trains, conflicts, M, delta = create_example_data()
    
    print(f"  Trains: {len(trains)}")
    print(f"  Conflict pairs: {len(conflicts)}")
    print(f"  Big-M: {M}")
    print(f"  Max deviation: {delta}s")
    
    print("\nBuilding MILP model...")
    cdr_model = RailwayCDRModel(trains, conflicts, M, delta)
    model = cdr_model.build_model()
    
    num_vars = len(model.variables())
    num_constrs = len(model.constraints)
    print(f"  Variables: {num_vars}")
    print(f"  Constraints: {num_constrs}")
    
    print("\nSolving...")
    status = cdr_model.solve(time_limit=60)
    print(f"  Status: {status}")
    
    print("\nResults:")
    cdr_model.print_solution()
    
    # Optional: Export model to LP file for inspection
    model.writeLP("railway_cdr.lp")
    print("\nModel exported to railway_cdr.lp")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## Key Features of the Implementation

### 1. **ETCS Level 2 DTG Modelling**
- Speed-dependent braking distances (`B_{i,r,s}(v)`)
- Train- and speed-dependent headways computed from braking curves
- Movement authority (MA) constraints ensuring safe separation

### 2. **Multiple Speed Profiles**
- Each train-section combination has multiple candidate speed profiles
- Binary selection variables ensure exactly one profile is chosen
- Speed consistency constraints between consecutive sections

### 3. **Switch-Specific Handling**
- Switches treated as atomic resources with extended blocking times
- Route locking and swinging time included in headways
- Distinction between switch and non-switch sections

### 4. **Disjunctive Conflict Constraints**
- Big-M formulation for train ordering decisions
- Speed-dependent separation times in constraints
- Efficient handling of multiple conflicting pairs

### 5. **Flexible Data Structures**
- Dataclasses for clean parameter organization
- Easy integration with real infrastructure data
- Example data generator for testing

### Usage Notes

1. **Replace example data** with actual railway network data including:
   - Real track topology and section lengths
   - Actual train characteristics (braking curves, speed profiles)
   - Real timetable data

2. **Solver selection**: The code tries Gurobi first (commercial, faster), falls back to CBC (free)

3. **Scaling considerations**: For large networks, consider:
   - Decomposition approaches (Benders, column generation)
   - Rolling horizon implementation
   - Preprocessing to reduce conflict pairs

4. **Calibration**: Adjust parameters like:
   - Big-M value (should be tight for efficiency)
   - Safety margins in headway calculations
   - Speed tolerance for consistency constraints

Introduction

Worldwide, railways are experiencing a continuously increasing travel demand. The existing railway networks have limited capacity and fewer and fewer extension possibilities due to the costly and land-consuming infrastructure. Especially at capacity bottlenecks such as in and around stations, extensions are often not available. To fulfil future railway demand in a different way, advanced signalling systems such as distance-to-go (DTG) systems are developed as capacityincreasing alternatives to conventional fixed-block multi-aspect signalling with automatic train protection systems.

In conventional fixed-block systems, the track is partitioned into blocks of fixed lengths which can be occupied by at most one train at a time.

The block entries are protected by trackside multi-aspect signals which indicate whether an approaching train can proceed, needs to start braking or is required to stop. The automatic train protection system supervises that the trains follow the signal aspects and intervenes when a train does not start braking after a brake indication. Hence, train separation distances are determined based on a number of blocks of fixed length.

Fixed-block DTG systems feature radio-based cab signalling and continuous braking curve supervision from the train front position to the block (or section) entry corresponding to the train’s end of movement authority (MA), i.e., the permission to move to a specific location under supervision. With this, brake indications no longer need to be provided at the entry of a block. Moreover, train separation distances become speed-dependent due to the approach distance to the first occupied block being based on the train’s absolute braking distance.

For effective railway operations, real-time traffic management is crucial. In case of small delays originating from variations in rolling stock, dwell times and driver behaviour, traffic management can apply rescheduling measures such as retiming, reordering and local rerouting to resolve track conflicts while minimising the delay propagation in the network. To support human dispatchers in taking mathematically optimised rescheduling decisions, conflict detection and resolution (CDR) models describing variants of the real-time railway traffic management or rescheduling problem are developed (Cacchiani et al., 2014; Pellegrini et al., 2014). In short, the problem can be formally described as follows: given a railway network and timetable together with delayed events, find a new timetable by rescheduling trains such that all track conflicts are resolved and total delay (or other relevant objective) is minimised.

The existing CDR models mostly refer to conventional fixed-block signalling systems. As a result, they are typically microscopic models that inherently rely on the discretisation of the track into fixed blocks. Moreover, they generally neglect changes in the speed profile to fit the adjusted timetable (Reynolds et al., 2022). Hence, these models cannot accurately capture the speed-dependent separation distances typical for DTG signalling due to the implementation of braking curve supervision (Versluis et al., 2024).

In this paper, we address the research gap regarding CDR for DTG signalling by developing a CDR model for DTG and applying it to assess the operational relevance of modelling CDR for DTG. To obtain a model that represents and identifies optimised rescheduling decisions for DTG railway operations, we propose enhancements for existing CDR models. The enhancements include the introduction of speed profile options and train blocking times considering train- and speed-dependent braking distances. These two enhancements are significant as they are crucial in enabling the modelling of train- and speed-dependent brake indication points in CDR models. As a proof of concept, we incorporate the enhancements into the state-of-the-art CDR model of RECIFE-MILP (Pellegrini et al., 2015), together with a distinction between switches and the rest of the track. The resulting model is assessed through a comparative analysis with the original one for conventional fixed-block signalling in two case studies, specifically in terms of total train delay and rescheduling decisions.

With this, the main contributions of the paper are:

A modelling approach for enhancing conflict detection and resolution models to apply to distance-to-go signalling, introducing train- and speed-dependent train separation and brake indication points.

A mixed-integer linear programming model for conflict detection and resolution under distance-to-go signalling, obtained by integrating distance-to-go principles into the state-of-the-art RECIFE-MILP model.

A comparative analysis illustrating the operational relevance of incorporating distance-to-go principles into conflict detection and resolution modelling, as different rescheduling decisions achieving reductions in total train delay are proposed.

The paper is organised as follows. In Section 2, the state-of-the-art related to the modelling of CDR for DTG signalling is provided.

Section 3 describes the enhancement approach for CDR models to describe DTG signalling.

The mathematical formulation of the fixed-block CDR model RECIFE-MILP enhanced for DTG signalling is presented in Section 4. Section 5 presents the results of the comparative analysis. Finally, Section 6 concludes the paper. State-of-the-art in conflict detection and resolution for distance-to-go signalling In this section, we provide an overview of the state-of-the-art relevant for the topic of modelling CDR under DTG signalling. Section 2.1 focuses on DTG signalling as the de-facto standard in the development of next-generation signalling systems. Section 2.2 provides an overview on modelling approaches for CDR existing in the literature.

2.1 Distance-to-go signalling systems In the development of next-generation signalling systems, DTG is the de-facto standard. For the mainline railways, DTG signalling is included within the European Train Control System (ETCS) and the Chinese Train Control System (CTCS). For metro lines, Communication-Based Train Control (CBTC) applies DTG signalling principles. Examples of deployed DTG systems are the fixed-block ETCS Level 2 with Trackside Train Detection (TTD) and the similar CTCS Level 3. The latter is designed for the Chinese high-speed (up to 300 km/h) railway lines (Xu et al., 2017). In this paper, we focus on ETCS Level 2 with TTD, hereafter referred to as ETCS L2, which is implemented on freight and passenger railways throughout the world (European Rail Supply Industry Association, 2022).

To enable cab signalling, ETCS L2 features radio communication between a radio block centre on the trackside and the trains as follows. The radio block centre receives train position information from a train. This information supports the request for a route extension to the interlocking system. Based on safety logic and input from TTD, the interlocking system sets and locks a new route for the train. As a next step, the radio block centre updates the MA before sending it to the train. With the received MA, the train recomputes and supervises a dynamic speed profile including continuous braking curves.

Corresponding to the braking curves, the brake indication point for a train can lie anywhere along the track. The end of authority, however, is consistently set at the end of a block or TTD section (TDS). The TDSs correspond to the parts of the track in which the presence of a train is automatically detected. Whether the end of authority corresponds to a block or TDS depends on the implemented ETCS L2 variant. It can also depend on whether it is on the open line, in a station or around switches. A schematic representation of the ETCS L2 system is provided in Figure 1. In the figure, two trains at the speed-dependent minimum separation distance are included.

Figure 1: Schematic layout of the minimum separation between two trains in a speed-distance diagram under ETCS L2 with (block) section boundaries, radio block centre (RBC) and radio communication (GSM-R). The separation is related to the brake indication point (IP) and the end of authority (EoA) depending on the braking curve.

Within ETCS and CTCS, more advanced application levels are being developed, but not yet deployed.

In particular, ETCS Level 2 with onboard train integrity monitoring (TIM), previously known as ETCS Level 3. This allows the end of authority to be located at the end of the last free virtual (non-physical) block, e.g., in ETCS Level 2 Virtual Block, or even at a safety margin behind the rear position of a moving train, e.g., in ETCS Level 2 Moving Block (European Railway Agency, 2016).

function.arguments:
{"description":"Develop a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for real-time railway conflict detection and resolution (CDR) under ETCS Level 2 distance-to-go (DTG) signalling, extending the RECIFE-MILP framework (Pellegrini et al., 2015) with train- and speed-dependent braking distances, multiple speed profiles per train, and a distinction between switches and the rest of the track.

Sets and indices:
- T: set of trains, indexed by i (and j for a second train).
- R_i: ordered set of route sections (track sections / TDS) of train i, indexed by r; r=1..|R_i|. The route includes the section where the train is located at the start of the rescheduling horizon.
- S_i = {(r,s)}: set of candidate speed profile options for train i on route section r, indexed by s in 1..n_{i,r}. Each speed profile option s for train i on section r is defined by an entry speed v^in_{i,r,s} and a (speed-dependent) traversal time.
- C: set of conflicting pairs (i,r,j,r') meaning that section r of train i and section r' of train j correspond to the same physical track resource (block section / TTD section) and the trains may conflict. This includes pairs of trains with common route sections.
- SW: subset of sections that are switches (turnouts); other sections are open line or platform track sections.

Parameters:
- t^0_{i,r}: scheduled (planned) arrival time of train i at the entry of section r from the original timetable.
- d^0_i: entrance delay of train i at the start of the horizon (delay at its first section).
- l_{i,r,s}: minimum running (traversal) time of train i on section r under speed profile s (depends on entry speed and section length, speed-dependent under DTG).
- f_i: scheduled dwell time of train i at the station located on its route (if any; otherwise 0); dwell is performed on a designated section.
- B_{i,r,s}(v): braking distance of train i when braking from speed v under profile s on section r. Under DTG/ETCS L2 the separation between two consecutive trains on the same track depends on the absolute braking distance of the following train: the following train must receive its movement authority (MA) such that its supervised braking curve ends at the end of authority (EoA) located at the end of the last free block section/TDS before the preceding train. The brake indication point can lie anywhere along the track and is speed-dependent.
- o_{i,r,j,r',s}: minimum separation (blocking) time headway required between train i occupying section r with speed profile s and the following train j entering the corresponding conflicting section r', computed from the speed-dependent braking distance B and the approach speed (train- and speed-dependent blocking time). For conventional fixed-block this would be a constant number of block traversals; here it varies with s.
- a_{i,r}: 1 if section r of train i is a switch (in SW), 0 otherwise.
- M: a sufficiently large constant (big-M).
- w_i: weight/priority of train i in the objective (assumption: equals 1 for all trains if not specified).
- delta: maximum allowed deviation from the scheduled arrival times (assumption, to bound the horizon).

Decision variables:
- t_{i,r} >= 0: continuous variable, arrival (entry) time of train i at section r (rescheduled).
- x_{i,r,s} in {0,1}: binary variable, 1 if train i traverses section r with speed profile s.
- y_{i,r,j,r'} in {0,1}: binary sequencing variable for each conflicting pair (i,r,j,r'), 1 if train i enters the shared resource before train j, 0 otherwise (disjunctive ordering variable).

Objective function:
Minimise the total weighted train delay at a relevant reference point (e.g., at the exit of the rescheduling horizon or at scheduled stops). For each train i, the delay is measured at the last section of its route: D_i = max(0, t_{i,last} - t^0_{i,last}). Since this is linear via t_{i,last} >= t^0_{i,last} when delays are nonnegative after optimisation, minimise sum_i w_i * (t_{i,|R_i|} - t^0_{i,|R_i|}). Alternatively use deviation variables e_i >= t_{i,|R_i|} - t^0_{i,|R_i|}, e_i >= 0 and minimise sum_i w_i e_i.

Constraints:
1. Speed profile selection: for each train i and each section r on its route, exactly one speed profile is chosen: sum_s x_{i,r,s} = 1.
2. Running time constraints (precedence along the route): t_{i,r+1} >= t_{i,r} + sum_s l_{i,r,s} x_{i,r,s} + f_{i,r} where f_{i,r} is the dwell time if r is a scheduled stop section (0 otherwise), for all i and r=1..|R_i|-1. Because x are binary and l are parameters, sum_s l_{i,r,s} x_{i,r,s} is linear.
3. Scheduled (timetable) lower bounds / no early departure: t_{i,r} >= t^0_{i,r} for all i and r where early running is not allowed (assumption: at least for the first section and scheduled stops). Also t_{i,1} >= d^0_i + t^0_{i,1} (entrance delay propagates). Optionally t_{i,r} <= t^0_{i,r} + delta.
4. Dwell time constraints at scheduled stops: t_{i,r+1} >= t_{i,r} + sum_s l_{i,r,s} x_{i,r,s} + f_i (included in constraint 2); departure no earlier than scheduled departure: t_{i,r+1} >= t^0_{i,r+1} at stops (assumption).
5. Conflict (disjunctive) constraints for each conflicting pair (i,r,j,r') in C: separation between trains on the same track resource, with train- and speed-dependent headway under DTG:
   t_{j,r'} >= t_{i,r} + sum_s o_{i,r,j,r',s} x_{i,r,s} - M (1 - y_{i,r,j,r'})
   t_{i,r} >= t_{j,r'} + sum_s o_{j,r',i,r,s'} x_{j,r',s'} - M y_{i,r,j,r'}
   where o_{i,r,j,r',s} is the minimum time headway between the entry of train i (with profile s) into section r and the entry of train j into section r' ensuring that j's braking curve under its MA ends at the EoA at the end of the last free TDS behind train i (speed-dependent separation). Note: these are linear since o are parameters and x binary.
6. Switch-specific constraints: for sections r in SW (switches), the switch (and its route locking) is treated as an atomic resource: while a train traverses a switch, no conflicting route over the same switch can be set. This is modelled by using a switch-specific separation time o^{SW} (including route setting/locking and swinging time) in constraint 5 for pairs involving switch sections, and by extending the occupancy: the conflicting resource is blocked from the entry of the train into the switch section until it clears the switch section (assumption: blocking time of a switch equals entry time plus traversal plus release time). Hence for (i,r,j,r') with r (or r') in SW use o^{SW}_{i,r,j,r',s} >= o_{i,r,j,r',s} (larger headway), and possibly additional pairwise constraints between the section preceding the switch and the switch section itself to model route locking before the train reaches the switch (assumption).
7. Speed consistency / braking feasibility across consecutive sections (assumption, linearised): the entry speed on section r+1 equals the exit speed of section r under the chosen profiles; to keep linearity, only compatible profile combinations are allowed, expressed with additional binaries or by defining profiles per section such that constraints sum_s v^out_{i,r,s} x_{i,r,s} = sum_s v^in_{i,r+1,s} x_{i,r+1,s} hold (linear equality in binaries if speeds are parameter values). Mark as optional/assumption.
8. Variable domains: t_{i,r} >= 0 (or >= lower bounds), x binary, y binary.

The model is a MILP with disjunctive (big-M) conflict constraints, binary speed-profile selection, and train- and speed-dependent separation headways capturing DTG braking-curve supervision, plus switch-specific blocking constraints distinguishing switches from the rest of the track. Output python code implementing the model (e.g., with PuLP or Gurobi), with placeholders/example data structures for the parameters."}
