# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Real-Time Railway Conflict Detection and Resolution under ETCS Level 2

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of track sections (blocks/TDS), indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{SW} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Subset of switch sections |
| $\mathcal{S}^{PT} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Subset of plain track sections ($\mathcal{S}^{SW} \cup \mathcal{S}^{PT} = \mathcal{S}$, $\mathcal{S}^{SW} \cap \mathcal{S}^{PT} = \emptyset$) |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of discrete speed profiles available to train $i$, indexed by $p$ (e.g., $\{1=\text{full}, 2=\text{medium}, 3=\text{low}\}$) |
| $\mathcal{R}_i = (s_i^1, s_i^2, \ldots, s_i^{n_i})$ | Ordered route of train $i$: sequence of sections |
| $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$ | The $k$-th section on train $i$'s route, $k = 1, \ldots, n_i$ |
| $\mathcal{K}_i = \{1, \ldots, n_i\}$ | Position index set for train $i$'s route |
| $\mathcal{S}_i$ | Set of sections traversed by train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{C}_s = \{(i,j) : i, j \in \mathcal{T},\; i \neq j,\; s \in \mathcal{S}_i \cap \mathcal{S}_j\}$ | Set of train pairs potentially conflicting on section $s$ |
| $\mathcal{A}_i \subseteq \mathcal{K}_i$ | Set of route positions where train $i$ has a scheduled stop (station) |
| $\mathcal{D}_i \subseteq \mathcal{K}_i$ | Set of route positions where delay is measured (station arrivals, network exit) |
| $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Set of sections where overtaking/reordering is permitted |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $r_i^{p}(s)$ | Running time of train $i$ on section $s$ under speed profile $p \in \mathcal{P}_i$ |
| $b_i^{p}(s)$ | Braking distance of train $i$ entering section $s$ under speed profile $p$ (train- and speed-dependent) |
| $v_i^{p}(s)$ | Entry speed of train $i$ on section $s$ under profile $p$ |
| $\tau_i^{p}(s)$ | Time for train $i$ to cover braking distance $b_i^{p}(s)$ at speed $v_i^{p}(s)$, i.e., $\tau_i^{p}(s) = b_i^{p}(s) / v_i^{p}(s)$ |
| $e_i$ | Earliest entry time of train $i$ into the network (release time) |
| $a_i^{sched}(k)$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at route position $k \in \mathcal{A}_i$ |
| $d_i^{sched}(k)$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from route position $k \in \mathcal{A}_i$ |
| $w_i^{min}(k)$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at route position $k \in \mathcal{A}_i$ |
| $L(s)$ | Length of section $s$ |
| $c_i(s)$ | Clearing time: time for train $i$ to fully clear section $s$ after its front reaches the section end (tail clearance) |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |
| $\omega_i(k)$ | Weight (priority) of delay for train $i$ at route position $k \in \mathcal{D}_i$ |
| $T^{hor}$ | Time horizon of the optimization |
| $\sigma_{ij}(s)$ | Minimum additional safety separation time between trains $i$ and $j$ on section $s$ (fixed safety margin) |

**Assumption 1.** The braking distance $b_i^p(s)$ depends on the train's braking curve (deceleration rate), the entry speed $v_i^p(s)$, and the gradient of section $s$. Under ETCS Level 2 DTG signalling, the movement authority extends to the end of the next section, so the follower must maintain a distance such that it can stop before the end of its authority.

**Assumption 2.** The time to cover the braking distance is approximated as $\tau_i^p(s) = b_i^p(s) / v_i^p(s)$, which is a conservative (constant-speed) approximation. This is a parameter computed offline for each $(i, p, s)$ combination.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Continuous Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $t_i^{arr}(k)$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at the **beginning** of the section at route position $k \in \mathcal{K}_i$ |
| $t_i^{dep}(k)$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from the **beginning** of the section at route position $k \in \mathcal{K}_i$ (i.e., the time train $i$ starts traversing section $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$) |
| $t_i^{exit}(k)$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Time at which train $i$ fully **exits** (clears) section $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$ |
| $\delta_i(k)$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Delay of train $i$ at route position $k \in \mathcal{D}_i$ (positive deviation from schedule) |

### 3.2 Binary Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_i^{p}(k)$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $= 1$ if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on section $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$; $0$ otherwise |
| $y_{ij}(s)$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $= 1$ if train $i$ enters section $s$ **before** train $j$; $= 0$ if $j$ enters before $i$ (sequencing variable for $(i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s$) |

---

## 4. Auxiliary Expressions (Linear)

The **effective running time** of train $i$ on section $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$:

$$\rho_i(k) = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} r_i^{p}(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \cdot x_i^{p}(k)$$

The **effective braking time** of train $i$ entering section $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$:

$$\beta_i(k) = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} \tau_i^{p}(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \cdot x_i^{p}(k)$$

Both are linear in the binary profile selection variables.

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$\min \quad Z = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{D}_i} \omega_i(k) \cdot \delta_i(k)$$

**Explanation:** Minimize the total weighted delay across all trains at designated measurement points (station arrivals, network exits). The weights $\omega_i(k)$ encode train priorities (e.g., high-speed passenger trains may have higher weights than freight trains).

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Speed Profile Selection (Exactly One Profile per Train per Section)

$$\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} x_i^{p}(k) = 1 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{1}$$

**Explanation:** Each train must select exactly one speed profile for each section on its route. This links the binary profile variables to the running time and braking distance expressions.

---

### 6.2 Temporal Propagation Along the Route (Running Time Constraints)

$$t_i^{arr}(k+1) = t_i^{dep}(k) + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} r_i^{p}(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \cdot x_i^{p}(k) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i : k < n_i \tag{2}$$

**Explanation:** The arrival time at the start of the next section equals the departure time from the current section plus the running time on the current section, which depends on the selected speed profile. This is linear because $r_i^p$ is a parameter and $x_i^p$ is a binary variable.

---

### 6.3 Section Exit (Clearing) Time

$$t_i^{exit}(k) = t_i^{dep}(k) + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} r_i^{p}(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \cdot x_i^{p}(k) + c_i(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{3}$$

**Explanation:** The exit time from a section is the departure time plus the running time plus the clearing time $c_i(s)$ (time for the tail of the train to clear the section after the front reaches the end).

---

### 6.4 Release Time Constraints (No Early Start)

$$t_i^{dep}(1) \geq e_i \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{4}$$

**Explanation:** Train $i$ cannot enter the network (depart from the start of its first section) before its release/entry time $e_i$.

---

### 6.5 Dwell Time Constraints at Scheduled Stops

$$t_i^{dep}(k) \geq t_i^{arr}(k) + w_i^{min}(k) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{A}_i \tag{5}$$

**Explanation:** At each scheduled stop, the train must dwell for at least the minimum dwell time $w_i^{min}(k)$ before departing.

---

### 6.6 Scheduled Departure Constraints (No Early Departure from Stops)

$$t_i^{dep}(k) \geq d_i^{sched}(k) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{A}_i \tag{6}$$

**Explanation:** A train cannot depart from a scheduled stop before its scheduled departure time. This enforces the timetable as a lower bound (retiming is allowed only as delays, not early departures).

**Assumption 3.** Early departures from stations are not permitted (standard in railway CDR). If early departures were allowed, this constraint would be relaxed.

---

### 6.7 Departure Equals Arrival at Non-Stop Sections

$$t_i^{dep}(k) = t_i^{arr}(k) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \setminus \mathcal{A}_i \tag{7}$$

**Explanation:** At sections where the train does not have a scheduled stop, the departure time equals the arrival time (no dwell).

---

### 6.8 Delay Definition Constraints

$$\delta_i(k) \geq t_i^{arr}(k) - a_i^{sched}(k) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{D}_i \tag{8}$$

$$\delta_i(k) \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{D}_i \tag{9}$$

**Explanation:** The delay $\delta_i(k)$ is the positive deviation of the actual arrival time from the scheduled arrival time. Since we minimize, $\delta_i(k)$ will take the value $\max(0, t_i^{arr}(k) - a_i^{sched}(k))$ at optimality.

---

### 6.9 Blocking Time / Separation Constraints under ETCS Level 2 DTG

For each section $s \in \mathcal{S}$ and each pair of trains $(i, j) \in \mathcal{C}_s$ sharing section $s$, let $k_i$ and $k_j$ be the route positions such that $\mathcal{R}_i(k_i) = s$ and $\mathcal{R}_j(k_j) = s$.

**Case A: Train $i$ leads, train $j$ follows** (enforced when $y_{ij}(s) = 1$):

$$t_j^{dep}(k_j) \geq t_i^{exit}(k_i) + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_j} \tau_j^{p}(s) \cdot x_j^{p}(k_j) + \sigma_{ij}(s) - M \cdot (1 - y_{ij}(s)) \tag{10a}$$

**Case B: Train $j$ leads, train $i$ follows** (enforced when $y_{ij}(s) = 0$):

$$t_i^{dep}(k_i) \geq t_j^{exit}(k_j) + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} \tau_i^{p}(s) \cdot x_i^{p}(k_i) + \sigma_{ji}(s) - M \cdot y_{ij}(s) \tag{10b}$$

**Explanation:** These are the core DTG blocking time constraints. Under ETCS Level 2 with distance-to-go signalling:

- When train $i$ leads ($y_{ij}(s) = 1$), constraint (10a) becomes active and (10b) is relaxed by the big-M term. The follower $j$ may enter section $s$ only after:
  1. The leader $i$ has fully cleared section $s$ (i.e., $t_i^{exit}(k_i)$), **plus**
  2. The time $\tau_j^p(s) = b_j^p(s)/v_j^p(s)$ needed for the follower $j$ to cover its speed-dependent braking distance (so that $j$'s braking curve does not violate the end of authority at the section end), **plus**
  3. A fixed safety margin $\sigma_{ij}(s)$.

- When train $j$ leads ($y_{ij}(s) = 0$), constraint (10b) becomes active instead, with the roles reversed.

- The binary variable $y_{ij}(s)$ determines the **sequencing** (order) of trains on section $s$. The big-M formulation creates a disjunctive constraint: exactly one of the two cases is enforced.

**Assumption 4.** The braking distance $b_j^p(s)$ is computed based on the entry speed $v_j^p(s)$ associated with the selected profile $p$, the train's deceleration capability, and the section gradient. Under DTG, the movement authority for the follower extends to the end of the section occupied by the leader, so the follower must be able to stop within that distance.

**Assumption 5.** For switch sections $s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW}$, an additional constraint may be needed to account for route setting and locking time. This is captured by a potentially larger $\sigma_{ij}(s)$ for switch sections.

---

### 6.10 Switch Section Route Compatibility (Optional but Recommended)

For switch sections $s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW}$, if trains $i$ and $j$ require **conflicting switch positions** (different routes through the switch), an additional switch re-setting time $\Delta^{SW}(s)$ is required:

$$t_j^{dep}(k_j) \geq t_i^{exit}(k_i) + \Delta^{SW}(s) - M \cdot (1 - y_{ij}(s)) \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s^{conflict},\; s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW} \tag{11a}$$

$$t_i^{dep}(k_i) \geq t_j^{exit}(k_j) + \Delta^{SW}(s) - M \cdot y_{ij}(s) \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s^{conflict},\; s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW} \tag{11b}$$

where $\mathcal{C}_s^{conflict} \subseteq \mathcal{C}_s$ is the set of train pairs requiring different switch positions on section $s$.

**Explanation:** When two consecutive trains need different switch alignments, additional time is needed for the switch to be re-positioned and locked. This is added on top of the normal separation.

---

### 6.11 Reordering Constraints (Optional — at Designated Locations)

For sections $s \in \mathcal{Q}$ (where reordering is permitted), the sequencing variables $y_{ij}(s)$ are **free binary variables** — the optimizer decides the order.

For sections $s \notin \mathcal{Q}$ (where reordering is **not** permitted), the order is fixed according to the original timetable or current state:

$$y_{ij}(s) = 1 \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s,\; s \notin \mathcal{Q},\; \text{if } i \text{ is scheduled before } j \text{ on } s \tag{12}$$

**Explanation:** At suitable locations (e.g., stations with multiple platforms, passing loops), the optimizer can choose to reorder trains. Elsewhere, the order is fixed to maintain feasibility and safety.

**Assumption 6.** Reordering is only allowed at sections in $\mathcal{Q}$. This is a modeling choice; in practice, $\mathcal{Q}$ typically includes station areas and dedicated overtaking points.

---

### 6.12 Retiming Constraints (Optional)

If retiming (adjusting scheduled times within limits) is permitted, introduce slack variables:

$$t_i^{dep}(k) \geq d_i^{sched}(k) - \epsilon_i^{dep}(k) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{A}_i \tag{13}$$

$$\epsilon_i^{dep}(k) \leq \bar{\epsilon} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{A}_i \tag{14}$$

where $\epsilon_i^{dep}(k) \geq 0$ is the allowed departure time adjustment and $\bar{\epsilon}$ is the maximum allowed retiming. A penalty term $\sum_{i,k} \gamma_i(k) \cdot \epsilon_i^{dep}(k)$ can be added to the objective.

**Assumption 7.** If retiming is not allowed, set $\bar{\epsilon} = 0$, which recovers constraint (6).

---

### 6.13 Time Horizon Constraints

$$t_i^{arr}(k) \leq T^{hor} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{15}$$

$$t_i^{dep}(k) \leq T^{hor} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{16}$$

**Explanation:** All event times must lie within the optimization time horizon.

---

### 6.14 Variable Domain Constraints

$$t_i^{arr}(k), \; t_i^{dep}(k), \; t_i^{exit}(k) \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{17}$$

$$\delta_i(k) \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{D}_i \tag{18}$$

$$x_i^{p}(k) \in \{0, 1\} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i,\; p \in \mathcal{P}_i \tag{19}$$

$$y_{ij}(s) \in \{0, 1\} \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S},\; (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s \tag{20}$$

---

## 7. Complete Model Summary

$$\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{D}_i} \omega_i(k) \cdot \delta_i(k) \\[6pt]
\text{s.t.} \quad
& \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} x_i^{p}(k) = 1 && \forall i, k \\
& t_i^{arr}(k+1) = t_i^{dep}(k) + \sum_{p} r_i^{p}(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \cdot x_i^{p}(k) && \forall i, k < n_i \\
& t_i^{exit}(k) = t_i^{dep}(k) + \sum_{p} r_i^{p}(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \cdot x_i^{p}(k) + c_i(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) && \forall i, k \\
& t_i^{dep}(1) \geq e_i && \forall i \\
& t_i^{dep}(k) \geq t_i^{arr}(k) + w_i^{min}(k) && \forall i, k \in \mathcal{A}_i \\
& t_i^{dep}(k) \geq d_i^{sched}(k) && \forall i, k \in \mathcal{A}_i \\
& t_i^{dep}(k) = t_i^{arr}(k) && \forall i, k \notin \mathcal{A}_i \\
& \delta_i(k) \geq t_i^{arr}(k) - a_i^{sched}(k) && \forall i, k \in \mathcal{D}_i \\
& t_j^{dep}(k_j) \geq t_i^{exit}(k_i) + \sum_{p} \tau_j^{p}(s) \cdot x_j^{p}(k_j) + \sigma_{ij}(s) - M(1 - y_{ij}(s)) && \forall s, (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s \\
& t_i^{dep}(k_i) \geq t_j^{exit}(k_j) + \sum_{p} \tau_i^{p}(s) \cdot x_i^{p}(k_i) + \sigma_{ji}(s) - M \cdot y_{ij}(s)) && \forall s, (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s \\
& y_{ij}(s) = 1 && \forall s \notin \mathcal{Q}, (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s, \; i \prec j \\
& t_i^{arr}(k), t_i^{dep}(k), t_i^{exit}(k) \in [0, T^{hor}] && \forall i, k \\
& \delta_i(k) \geq 0 && \forall i, k \in \mathcal{D}_i \\
& x_i^{p}(k) \in \{0,1\} && \forall i, k, p \\
& y_{ij}(s) \in \{0,1\} && \forall s, (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s
\end{aligned}$$

---

## 8. Explanation of Model Elements

### 8.1 Microscopic Network Representation
The network is modeled at the **microscopic level** as a set of track sections (blocks or Track Detection Sections, TDS). Each section is either a **switch section** (containing points/turnouts) or a **plain track section**. This distinction matters because switch sections require additional route-setting time and may have different speed restrictions.

### 8.2 Speed Profile Selection
Each train can choose from a finite set of speed profiles on each section. The profile determines:
- **Running time** $r_i^p(s)$: lower speed → longer running time
- **Braking distance** $b_i^p(s)$: lower entry speed → shorter braking distance → smaller required headway

This creates a trade-off: a slower profile increases the train's own running time but may reduce the required separation from the leader, potentially reducing overall delay in congested situations.

### 8.3 DTG Blocking Time Logic
Under ETCS Level 2 with distance-to-go signalling:
- The **movement authority (MA)** for a train extends to the end of the section ahead (or beyond, depending on the radio block center's grant).
- The **follower** must maintain sufficient distance so that its **braking curve** (from its current speed to a stop) does not exceed the end of its MA.
- The constraint (10a)/(10b) ensures: the follower enters section $s$ only after the leader has cleared it **plus** the time the follower needs to cover its braking distance. This is the **speed-dependent headway**.

### 8.4 Big-M Disjunctive Formulation
For each pair of trains sharing a section, exactly one of two orderings is possible:
- $y_{ij}(s) = 1$: train $i$ goes first → constraint (10a) is active, (10b) is relaxed
- $y_{ij}(s) = 0$: train $j$ goes first → constraint (10b) is active, (10a) is relaxed

The big-M constant must be chosen large enough to relax the inactive constraint but not so large as to cause numerical issues. A safe choice is $M = T^{hor} + \max_{i,p,s} \tau_i^p(s) + \max_{i,j,s} \sigma_{ij}(s)$.

### 8.5 Conflict Detection and Resolution
- **Detection**: Conflicts arise when the separation constraints (10a)/(10b) would be violated under the current timetable/ordering.
- **Resolution**: The optimizer resolves conflicts by:
  1. **Reordering**: choosing optimal values for $y_{ij}(s)$ at locations where reordering is allowed
  2. **Retiming**: adjusting departure/arrival times within timetable constraints
  3. **Speed profile adjustment**: selecting slower profiles to reduce braking distances and required headways

### 8.6 Linearity
All constraints are linear in the decision variables:
- Running times and braking times are **linear combinations** of binary profile variables with constant coefficients.
- The disjunctive constraints use the standard **big-M** technique, which is linear.
- Delay definitions use **linear inequalities** (the max function is captured by the minimization objective).
- No products of variables appear anywhere in the model.

---

## 9. Assumptions Summary

| # | Assumption |
|---|-----------|
| 1 | Braking distances are precomputed parameters based on train characteristics, entry speed, and section gradient. |
| 2 | Braking time $\tau_i^p(s) = b_i^p(s)/v_i^p(s)$ is a conservative constant-speed approximation. |
| 3 | Early departures from scheduled stops are not permitted. |
| 4 | Under DTG, the movement authority extends to the end of the next section; the follower must stop within this distance. |
| 5 | Switch sections may require additional route-setting time $\Delta^{SW}(s)$. |
| 6 | Reordering is only allowed at designated sections $\mathcal{Q}$. |
| 7 | Retiming is optional and bounded by $\bar{\epsilon}$. |
| 8 | Each train follows a fixed route (no rerouting); only reordering, retiming, and speed profile changes are allowed. |
| 9 | The clearing time $c_i(s)$ accounts for the train length and is a fixed parameter. |
| 10 | The model is solved in a rolling-horizon fashion for real-time application, with $e_i$ updated to reflect the current state. |

Model 3:
# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Real-Time Railway Conflict Detection and Resolution under ETCS Level 2 DTG Signalling

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of track sections (blocks/TDS), indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{SW} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Subset of switch sections |
| $\mathcal{S}^{PT} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Subset of plain track sections ($\mathcal{S}^{SW} \cup \mathcal{S}^{PT} = \mathcal{S}$, $\mathcal{S}^{SW} \cap \mathcal{S}^{PT} = \emptyset$) |
| $\mathcal{R}_i = (s_{i,1}, s_{i,2}, \ldots, s_{i,n_i})$ | Ordered route (sequence of sections) for train $i$, with $n_i = |\mathcal{R}_i|$ |
| $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$ | The $k$-th section on the route of train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of discrete speed profiles available to train $i$, indexed by $p$ (e.g., $\mathcal{P}_i = \{\text{full}, \text{medium}, \text{low}\}$) |
| $\mathcal{ST}_i \subseteq \{1, \ldots, n_i\}$ | Indices of route positions of train $i$ corresponding to scheduled stops (stations) |
| $\mathcal{E}_i$ | Index of the first section on train $i$'s route (entry point), i.e., position $k=1$ |
| $\mathcal{X}_i$ | Index of the last section on train $i$'s route (exit point), i.e., position $k=n_i$ |
| $\mathcal{C}_s = \{(i,k) : \mathcal{R}_i(k) = s\}$ | Set of train-route-position pairs that traverse section $s$ |
| $\mathcal{PAIRS}_s = \{((i,k),(j,l)) : (i,k),(j,l) \in \mathcal{C}_s,\; i \neq j\}$ | Ordered pairs of distinct trains sharing section $s$ |
| $\mathcal{W}$ | Set of delay measurement points $(i, k)$ where delay is penalized (e.g., station arrivals, network exits) |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $r_{i,k,p}$ | Running time of train $i$ on its $k$-th route section under speed profile $p \in \mathcal{P}_i$ |
| $b_{i,k,p}$ | Braking distance (expressed as additional time in seconds) of train $i$ entering its $k$-th route section under speed profile $p$; this is the time needed to cover the braking distance from the entry speed associated with profile $p$ |
| $e_i$ | Release (entry) time of train $i$ into the network (scheduled or actual, whichever is later) |
| $a^{\text{sched}}_{i,k}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at the end of its $k$-th route section (defined for $k \in \mathcal{ST}_i$ or $k = n_i$) |
| $d^{\text{sched}}_{i,k}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from its $k$-th route section (defined for $k \in \mathcal{ST}_i$) |
| $w^{\min}_{i,k}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at its $k$-th route section (for $k \in \mathcal{ST}_i$) |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |
| $\omega_{i,k}$ | Weight (priority) of delay for train $i$ at measurement point $(i,k) \in \mathcal{W}$ |
| $L_s$ | Length of section $s$ (used to compute $b_{i,k,p}$ offline) |
| $v^{\text{entry}}_{i,k,p}$ | Entry speed of train $i$ into its $k$-th section under profile $p$ (used offline to compute $b_{i,k,p}$) |
| $T^{\text{setup}}_s$ | Route setup/locking time for switch section $s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW}$ (additional separation time) |
| $T^{\text{release}}_s$ | Route release/unlocking time for switch section $s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW}$ |

> **Assumption (A1):** The braking distance parameter $b_{i,k,p}$ is pre-computed as a *time* quantity: $b_{i,k,p} = \text{BD}(v^{\text{entry}}_{i,k,p}) / v^{\text{entry}}_{i,k,p}$ where $\text{BD}(\cdot)$ is the train-specific braking curve under ETCS Level 2. This converts the distance-to-go constraint into a time-based separation, which is standard in the RECIFE-MILP framework.

> **Assumption (A2):** All running times $r_{i,k,p}$ are deterministic and known (no stochastic disturbances within the optimization horizon; the model is re-solved in a rolling-horizon fashion).

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Continuous Variables (Event Times)

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $t^{\text{in}}_{i,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Time at which train $i$ **enters** its $k$-th route section |
| $t^{\text{out}}_{i,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Time at which train $i$ **exits** (clears) its $k$-th route section |
| $d_{i,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Delay of train $i$ at measurement point $(i,k) \in \mathcal{W}$ (positive deviation from schedule) |

### 3.2 Binary Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,k,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $= 1$ if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on its $k$-th route section; $0$ otherwise |
| $y_{(i,k),(j,l)}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Sequencing variable for trains $i$ and $j$ on shared section $s = \mathcal{R}_i(k) = \mathcal{R}_j(l)$: $= 1$ if train $i$ enters section $s$ **before** train $j$; $= 0$ if $j$ enters before $i$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \quad Z = \sum_{(i,k) \in \mathcal{W}} \omega_{i,k} \cdot d_{i,k}
$$

**Explanation:** Minimize the total weighted delay across all designated measurement points (station arrivals, network exits). Weights $\omega_{i,k}$ can encode train priority (e.g., high-speed vs. freight) or passenger counts.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Speed Profile Selection (Exactly One Profile per Train per Section)

$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} x_{i,k,p} = 1 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k = 1, \ldots, n_i \tag{1}
$$

**Explanation:** Each train must select exactly one speed profile for each section on its route. This links the binary profile choice to the running time and braking distance parameters.

---

### 5.2 Running Time / Section Traversal Constraints

$$
t^{\text{out}}_{i,k} = t^{\text{in}}_{i,k} + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} r_{i,k,p} \cdot x_{i,k,p} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k = 1, \ldots, n_i \tag{2}
$$

**Explanation:** The exit time from a section equals the entry time plus the running time, which is determined by the selected speed profile. Since exactly one $x_{i,k,p} = 1$ (constraint (1)), the summation picks exactly one running time value. This is linear because $r_{i,k,p}$ is a parameter and $x_{i,k,p}$ is a binary variable.

---

### 5.3 Route Continuity Constraints

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{i,k+1} = t^{\text{out}}_{i,k} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k = 1, \ldots, n_i - 1,\; k \notin \mathcal{ST}_i \tag{3}
$$

**Explanation:** For non-stop sections, the entry time into the next section equals the exit time from the previous section (no dwell). For stop sections, this is replaced by the dwell time constraints (5.5).

---

### 5.4 Release Time (No Early Start) Constraints

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{i,1} \geq e_i \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{4}
$$

**Explanation:** Train $i$ cannot enter the network (its first section) before its release time $e_i$, which is the maximum of the scheduled entry time and the actual ready time (in real-time applications).

---

### 5.5 Dwell Time Constraints at Scheduled Stops

For each $i \in \mathcal{T}$ and $k \in \mathcal{ST}_i$:

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{i,k+1} \geq t^{\text{out}}_{i,k} + w^{\min}_{i,k} \tag{5}
$$

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{i,k+1} \geq d^{\text{sched}}_{i,k} \tag{6}
$$

**Explanation:** Constraint (5) enforces the minimum dwell time at a station stop: the train cannot depart (enter the next section) until at least $w^{\min}_{i,k}$ time units after arriving (exiting the previous section). Constraint (6) ensures the train does not depart before its scheduled departure time (no early departure from stations).

> **Assumption (A3):** For sections that are not scheduled stops ($k \notin \mathcal{ST}_i$), the dwell time is zero and constraint (3) applies.

---

### 5.6 Blocking Time / Separation Constraints under DTG Signalling (Big-M Disjunctive Constraints)

For each section $s \in \mathcal{S}$ and each ordered pair $((i,k),(j,l)) \in \mathcal{PAIRS}_s$ where $s = \mathcal{R}_i(k) = \mathcal{R}_j(l)$:

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{j,l} \geq t^{\text{out}}_{i,k} + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_j} b_{j,l,p} \cdot x_{j,l,p} + \mathbb{1}[s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW}] \cdot (T^{\text{setup}}_s + T^{\text{release}}_s) - M \cdot (1 - y_{(i,k),(j,l)}) \tag{7}
$$

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{i,k} \geq t^{\text{out}}_{j,l} + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} b_{i,k,p} \cdot x_{i,k,p} + \mathbb{1}[s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW}] \cdot (T^{\text{setup}}_s + T^{\text{release}}_s) - M \cdot y_{(i,k),(j,l)} \tag{8}
$$

**Explanation:** These are the core conflict resolution constraints implementing the DTG blocking time logic:

- **When $y_{(i,k),(j,l)} = 1$** (train $i$ leads, train $j$ follows): Constraint (7) is active and requires that follower $j$ enters section $s$ only after:
  - Leader $i$ has **cleared** section $s$ ($t^{\text{out}}_{i,k}$), **plus**
  - The **speed-dependent braking distance time** of follower $j$ ($\sum_p b_{j,l,p} \cdot x_{j,l,p}$), which depends on the profile selected by $j$ for this section, **plus**
  - If $s$ is a switch section, additional **route setup and release times** ($T^{\text{setup}}_s + T^{\text{release}}_s$).
  
  Constraint (8) is deactivated by the big-M term.

- **When $y_{(i,k),(j,l)} = 0$** (train $j$ leads, train $i$ follows): Constraint (8) is active and constraint (7) is deactivated, with the symmetric condition.

- The **DTG-specific feature** is that the separation depends on the **follower's** braking distance (determined by its selected speed profile), not a fixed headway. Under ETCS Level 2, the follower's End of Authority (EOA) is at the end of the section ahead of the leader's position, so the follower must maintain a distance equal to its braking curve from that EOA.

> **Assumption (A4):** The big-M constant is chosen as $M \geq \max_{i,k}\{t^{\text{out,max}}_{i,k}\} + \max_{j,l,p}\{b_{j,l,p}\} + \max_s\{T^{\text{setup}}_s + T^{\text{release}}_s\}$, i.e., larger than any possible relevant time difference. In practice, $M$ can be set to the scheduling horizon length.

> **Assumption (A5):** For switch sections, the additional setup/release times account for the interlocking locking and releasing the switch. For plain track sections, $\mathbb{1}[s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW}] = 0$ and no additional time is added.

---

### 5.7 Delay Definition Constraints

For each $(i,k) \in \mathcal{W}$:

$$
d_{i,k} \geq t^{\text{out}}_{i,k} - a^{\text{sched}}_{i,k} \tag{9}
$$

$$
d_{i,k} \geq 0 \tag{10}
$$

**Explanation:** The delay at a measurement point is the positive deviation of the actual arrival time (exit from the section) from the scheduled arrival time. Since we minimize a weighted sum of delays with non-negative weights, $d_{i,k}$ will take the value $\max(0, t^{\text{out}}_{i,k} - a^{\text{sched}}_{i,k})$ at optimality.

---

### 5.8 Optional Reordering Constraints

> **Assumption (A6):** Reordering (overtaking) is only possible at designated locations (stations with multiple platforms, passing loops). Let $\mathcal{O} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ be the set of sections where overtaking/reordering is permitted.

For sections $s \notin \mathcal{O}$ where trains $i$ and $j$ share the section and train $i$ is scheduled before train $j$:

$$
y_{(i,k),(j,l)} = 1 \quad \forall s \notin \mathcal{O},\; ((i,k),(j,l)) \in \mathcal{PAIRS}_s,\; a^{\text{sched}}_{i,k} < a^{\text{sched}}_{j,l} \tag{11}
$$

**Explanation:** At sections where reordering is not allowed, the original timetable order is preserved. At sections in $\mathcal{O}$, the sequencing variables $y$ remain free, allowing the optimizer to choose the order.

> **Assumption (A7):** This constraint is optional. If full reordering flexibility is desired everywhere, constraint (11) is simply omitted.

---

### 5.9 Retiming Constraints (Optional)

> **Assumption (A8):** Retiming refers to adjusting departure times at stations beyond the minimum dwell time, effectively holding a train to resolve a conflict downstream.

For each $i \in \mathcal{T}$ and $k \in \mathcal{ST}_i$, introduce an optional continuous variable:

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $h_{i,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Additional holding time of train $i$ at stop $k$ beyond the minimum dwell |

Then constraint (5) is modified to:

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{i,k+1} = t^{\text{out}}_{i,k} + w^{\min}_{i,k} + h_{i,k} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{ST}_i \tag{5'}
$$

And an upper bound on holding can be imposed:

$$
h_{i,k} \leq h^{\max}_{i,k} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{ST}_i \tag{12}
$$

**Explanation:** Retiming is naturally captured by the dwell time constraints: the optimizer can choose to hold a train longer at a station (increasing $h_{i,k}$) to resolve a downstream conflict. The equality in (5') replaces the inequality (5) when retiming is modeled explicitly. The bound (12) prevents excessive holding.

---

### 5.10 Variable Domain Constraints

$$
t^{\text{in}}_{i,k} \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k = 1, \ldots, n_i \tag{13}
$$

$$
t^{\text{out}}_{i,k} \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k = 1, \ldots, n_i \tag{14}
$$

$$
d_{i,k} \geq 0 \quad \forall (i,k) \in \mathcal{W} \tag{15}
$$

$$
x_{i,k,p} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k = 1, \ldots, n_i,\; p \in \mathcal{P}_i \tag{16}
$$

$$
y_{(i,k),(j,l)} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S},\; ((i,k),(j,l)) \in \mathcal{PAIRS}_s \tag{17}
$$

$$
h_{i,k} \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{ST}_i \tag{18}
$$

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

$$
\min \quad Z = \sum_{(i,k) \in \mathcal{W}} \omega_{i,k} \cdot d_{i,k}
$$

**subject to:**

| Constraint | Description | Reference |
|------------|-------------|-----------|
| (1) | Profile selection (exactly one per train per section) | §5.1 |
| (2) | Running time linking (profile-dependent) | §5.2 |
| (3) | Route continuity (non-stop sections) | §5.3 |
| (4) | Release time (no early start) | §5.4 |
| (5) or (5') | Minimum dwell time at stops | §5.5, §5.9 |
| (6) | No early departure from stations | §5.5 |
| (7), (8) | DTG blocking time / separation (big-M disjunctive) | §5.6 |
| (9), (10) | Delay definition | §5.7 |
| (11) | Reordering restrictions (optional) | §5.8 |
| (12) | Maximum holding time (optional) | §5.9 |
| (13)–(18) | Variable domains | §5.10 |

---

## 7. Model Properties and Remarks

### Linearity
All constraints are linear in the decision variables:
- Constraints (1), (3), (4), (5), (6), (9), (10), (11), (12) are standard linear (in)equalities.
- Constraint (2) is linear because $r_{i,k,p}$ is a parameter multiplied by binary variable $x_{i,k,p}$.
- Constraints (7) and (8) are linear because $b_{j,l,p}$ is a parameter multiplied by binary variable $x_{j,l,p}$, and the big-M term involves only binary variable $y$.

### Complexity
The model is a MILP with:
- $O(|\mathcal{T}| \cdot \bar{n} \cdot |\mathcal{P}|)$ binary profile variables, where $\bar{n}$ is the average route length and $|\mathcal{P}|$ is the average number of profiles.
- $O(|\mathcal{T}|^2 \cdot \bar{n})$ binary sequencing variables (in the worst case, all pairs of trains share all sections).
- $O(|\mathcal{T}| \cdot \bar{n})$ continuous time variables.

### DTG-Specific Features
The key innovation over fixed-block CDR models is in constraints (7)–(8): the separation between trains is **not a fixed headway time** but depends on the **follower's braking distance**, which is a function of the selected speed profile. This captures the essential DTG behaviour where:
- A faster-following train needs more separation (longer braking distance).
- Reducing the follower's speed profile (selecting a lower profile) reduces the required separation, enabling tighter following at the cost of longer running time.
- This trade-off is endogenously optimized by the model.

### Rolling Horizon Implementation
In real-time application, the model is solved repeatedly (every 30–120 seconds) with updated release times $e_i$ and current train positions, following the RECIFE-MILP framework. Trains that have already entered a section have their corresponding variables fixed to observed values.

Develop a complete mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model for real-time railway conflict detection and resolution (CDR) under ETCS Level 2 distance-to-go (DTG) signalling, extending the RECIFE-MILP framework. The model must include: (1) a microscopic railway network represented as a set of track sections (blocks/TDS) with a distinction between switch sections and plain track sections; (2) a set of trains, each with a route (ordered sequence of sections), an entry time into the network, scheduled arrival/departure times at stations, minimum dwell times, and running times per section that depend on the chosen speed profile; (3) a finite set of discrete speed profile options per train per section (e.g., full speed, medium, low), where each profile determines the running time on the section and the train- and speed-dependent braking distance; (4) blocking time / separation constraints under DTG: the minimum headway between two trains on the same section depends on the follower train's braking distance from its entry speed (given by the selected speed profile), i.e., the follower may enter a section only after the leader has cleared the section ahead (end of authority at section end) plus the time needed to cover the speed-dependent braking distance; use big-M disjunctive constraints with binary sequencing variables for each pair of trains sharing a section; (5) speed profile selection variables (binary, exactly one profile per train per section) linking running times and braking distances linearly; (6) timetable constraints: arrival/departure time variables at each section, release times (no early start before scheduled/actual entry), dwell time constraints at stops, and delay definitions (positive deviation from schedule); (7) optional reordering at suitable locations and retiming decisions; (8) objective: minimize total weighted train delay at relevant points (e.g., arrivals at stations or network exits). All constraints must be linear. Provide full notation: sets, parameters, decision variables (continuous event times, binary sequencing variables, binary profile selection variables), objective function, and constraints, with assumptions clearly marked.

response.content:
# Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Model for Real-Time Railway Conflict Detection and Resolution under ETCS Level 2

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of track sections (blocks/TDS), indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{SW} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Subset of switch sections |
| $\mathcal{S}^{PT} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Subset of plain track sections ($\mathcal{S} = \mathcal{S}^{SW} \cup \mathcal{S}^{PT}$, $\mathcal{S}^{SW} \cap \mathcal{S}^{PT} = \emptyset$) |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of discrete speed profiles available to train $i$, indexed by $p$ (e.g., $\{1=\text{full}, 2=\text{medium}, 3=\text{low}\}$) |
| $\mathcal{R}_i = (s_i^1, s_i^2, \ldots, s_i^{n_i})$ | Ordered route of train $i$: sequence of sections |
| $n_i$ | Number of sections on train $i$'s route |
| $\mathcal{K}_i = \{1, 2, \ldots, n_i\}$ | Position indices on train $i$'s route |
| $\mathcal{K}_i^{stop} \subseteq \mathcal{K}_i$ | Positions where train $i$ has a scheduled stop |
| $\mathcal{K}_i^{arr} \subseteq \mathcal{K}_i$ | Positions where arrival delay is measured (station arrivals, network exit) |
| $\mathcal{C}_s = \{(i,k) : s_i^k = s\}$ | Set of train-position pairs that traverse section $s$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_s^{pair} = \{((i,k),(j,l)) : (i,k),(j,l) \in \mathcal{C}_s, \; i \neq j\}$ | Ordered pairs of distinct trains sharing section $s$ |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $r_i^{entry}$ | Release (entry) time of train $i$ into the network (scheduled or actual) |
| $t_{i,k}^{arr,*}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at the end of section $s_i^k$ (for $k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{stop}$ or $k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{arr}$) |
| $t_{i,k}^{dep,*}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from section $s_i^k$ (for $k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{stop}$) |
| $d_{i,k}^{min}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at stop position $k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{stop}$ |
| $\tau_{i,k,p}$ | Running time of train $i$ on section $s_i^k$ under speed profile $p \in \mathcal{P}_i$ |
| $b_{i,k,p}$ | Braking distance of train $i$ when entering section $s_i^k$ at the speed prescribed by profile $p$ |
| $L_s$ | Length of section $s$ |
| $v_{i,k,p}$ | Entry speed of train $i$ into section $s_i^k$ under profile $p$ |
| $\beta_{i,k,p}$ | Time for train $i$ to cover braking distance $b_{i,k,p}$ from entry speed $v_{i,k,p}$ (computed as $\beta_{i,k,p} = b_{i,k,p} / v_{i,k,p}$ or from deceleration tables) |
| $h_s^{clear}$ | Additional clearing time for section $s$ (safety margin, switch setting time if $s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW}$) |
| $w_{i,k}$ | Weight (priority) of delay for train $i$ at measurement point $k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{arr}$ |
| $M$ | Sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |
| $T^{max}$ | Time horizon upper bound |

**Assumption (A1):** The braking time $\beta_{i,k,p}$ is precomputed for each train, section, and profile from the train's braking curves (e.g., using the ETCS braking model or a simplified kinematic model), so it enters the MILP as a constant parameter.

**Assumption (A2):** Under DTG signalling, the follower train's movement authority extends to the end of the section occupied by the leader. The follower must maintain a separation such that it can stop before the end of its authority. This translates to a time headway equal to the time needed to traverse the braking distance at the follower's entry speed.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Continuous Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $a_{i,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at the **end** of section $s_i^k$ (i.e., at the boundary between $s_i^k$ and $s_i^{k+1}$), for $k \in \mathcal{K}_i$ |
| $dep_{i,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from the **start** of section $s_i^k$ (i.e., entry into section $s_i^k$), for $k \in \mathcal{K}_i$ |
| $\delta_{i,k}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Delay (positive deviation) of train $i$ at measurement point $k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{arr}$ |

### 3.2 Binary Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,k,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $= 1$ if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on section $s_i^k$; $0$ otherwise |
| $y_{(i,k),(j,l)}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | Sequencing variable for pair $((i,k),(j,l)) \in \mathcal{P}_s^{pair}$: $= 1$ if train $i$ enters section $s$ before train $j$; $= 0$ if $j$ enters before $i$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the total weighted delay at all designated measurement points:

$$\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{arr}} w_{i,k} \cdot \delta_{i,k}$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Speed Profile Selection (Exactly One Profile per Train per Section)

$$\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} x_{i,k,p} = 1 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{1}$$

**Explanation:** Each train must select exactly one speed profile for each section on its route.

---

### 5.2 Running Time Linking (Profile-Dependent Travel Times)

The running time of train $i$ on section $s_i^k$ is determined by the selected profile. Define the effective running time as:

$$a_{i,k} = dep_{i,k} + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} \tau_{i,k,p} \cdot x_{i,k,p} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{2}$$

**Explanation:** Since exactly one $x_{i,k,p} = 1$, the summation picks the running time corresponding to the chosen profile. This is linear because $\tau_{i,k,p}$ is a parameter.

---

### 5.3 Release Time Constraints (No Early Start)

$$dep_{i,1} \geq r_i^{entry} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{3}$$

**Explanation:** Train $i$ cannot enter its first section before its release (entry) time.

---

### 5.4 Route Continuity (Departure from Previous Section)

For sections that are **not** scheduled stops ($k \notin \mathcal{K}_i^{stop}$):

$$dep_{i,k+1} = a_{i,k} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \setminus \mathcal{K}_i^{stop}, \; k < n_i \tag{4}$$

**Explanation:** If there is no scheduled stop, the train departs immediately upon arrival at the section boundary.

---

### 5.5 Dwell Time Constraints at Scheduled Stops

For positions with a scheduled stop ($k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{stop}$):

$$dep_{i,k+1} \geq a_{i,k} + d_{i,k}^{min} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{stop}, \; k < n_i \tag{5}$$

$$dep_{i,k+1} \geq t_{i,k}^{dep,*} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{stop}, \; k < n_i \tag{6}$$

**Explanation:** Constraint (5) enforces the minimum dwell time. Constraint (6) ensures the train does not depart before its scheduled departure time (no early departure from stations).

---

### 5.6 Delay Definition

$$\delta_{i,k} \geq a_{i,k} - t_{i,k}^{arr,*} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{arr} \tag{7}$$

$$\delta_{i,k} \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{arr} \tag{8}$$

**Explanation:** The delay is the positive deviation of the actual arrival time from the scheduled arrival time. Since we minimize, $\delta_{i,k}$ will equal $\max(0, a_{i,k} - t_{i,k}^{arr,*})$ at optimality.

---

### 5.7 Blocking Time / Separation Constraints under DTG Signalling

For each pair of trains $((i,k),(j,l)) \in \mathcal{P}_s^{pair}$ sharing section $s$:

**Case 1: Train $i$ precedes train $j$ on section $s$** ($y_{(i,k),(j,l)} = 1$):

Train $j$ may enter section $s$ only after:
- Train $i$ has cleared section $s$ (arrived at the end of $s$), **plus**
- A clearing time $h_s^{clear}$, **plus**
- The time for train $j$ to cover its braking distance from its entry speed (which depends on $j$'s selected profile on section $s$).

$$dep_{j,l} \geq a_{i,k} + h_s^{clear} + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_j} \beta_{j,l,p} \cdot x_{j,l,p} - M \cdot (1 - y_{(i,k),(j,l)}) \tag{9}$$

**Case 2: Train $j$ precedes train $i$ on section $s$** ($y_{(i,k),(j,l)} = 0$):

$$dep_{i,k} \geq a_{j,l} + h_s^{clear} + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} \beta_{i,k,p} \cdot x_{i,k,p} - M \cdot y_{(i,k),(j,l)} \tag{10}$$

**Explanation:** These are the core disjunctive constraints. Exactly one of them is active depending on the sequencing variable $y$. The braking time term $\sum_p \beta_{j,l,p} \cdot x_{j,l,p}$ is linear because $\beta_{j,l,p}$ is a parameter and $x_{j,l,p}$ is a binary variable. The summation selects the braking time corresponding to the follower's chosen speed profile.

**Assumption (A3):** The braking distance $b_{i,k,p}$ is always less than or equal to the section length $L_s$ for all profiles that are allowed on section $s$. Profiles violating this are excluded from $\mathcal{P}_i$ for that section.

**Assumption (A4):** For switch sections ($s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW}$), the clearing time $h_s^{clear}$ includes the time needed to reset the switch for the conflicting route. For plain track sections, $h_s^{clear}$ is a smaller safety margin.

---

### 5.8 Switch Section Compatibility (Optional but Recommended)

For switch sections, if two trains require **conflicting switch positions** (different routes through the switch), an additional constraint ensures the switch is not set simultaneously. Define:

- $\theta_{i,k} \in \{0, 1, \ldots\}$: the switch position required by train $i$ at section $s_i^k$ (parameter derived from the route).

For pairs $((i,k),(j,l)) \in \mathcal{P}_s^{pair}$ with $s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW}$ and $\theta_{i,k} \neq \theta_{j,l}$:

$$dep_{j,l} \geq a_{i,k} + h_s^{switch} - M \cdot (1 - y_{(i,k),(j,l)}) \tag{11}$$

$$dep_{i,k} \geq a_{j,l} + h_s^{switch} - M \cdot y_{(i,k),(j,l)} \tag{12}$$

where $h_s^{switch} \geq h_s^{clear}$ is the total time for clearing and re-setting the switch.

**Assumption (A5):** Constraints (11)–(12) replace constraints (9)–(10) for conflicting switch movements (i.e., use the larger of the two headway values). For non-conflicting movements (same switch position), constraints (9)–(10) suffice.

---

### 5.9 Time Horizon Bounds

$$dep_{i,k} \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{13}$$

$$a_{i,k} \leq T^{max} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{14}$$

---

## 6. Complete Model Summary

$$\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_i^{arr}} w_{i,k} \cdot \delta_{i,k}$$

**Subject to:**

| Constraint | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| (1) | Exactly one speed profile per train per section |
| (2) | Running time linking via profile selection |
| (3) | Release time (no early network entry) |
| (4) | Route continuity at non-stop positions |
| (5) | Minimum dwell time at stops |
| (6) | No early departure from scheduled stops |
| (7)–(8) | Delay definition (positive deviation) |
| (9)–(10) | DTG blocking time / separation with speed-dependent braking headway |
| (11)–(12) | Switch section compatibility for conflicting routes |
| (13)–(14) | Time bounds |

---

## 7. Key Assumptions Summary

| ID | Assumption |
|----|------------|
| **A1** | Braking times $\beta_{i,k,p}$ are precomputed constants from ETCS braking curves |
| **A2** | DTG separation = leader clears section + follower covers braking distance |
| **A3** | All allowed profiles have braking distance ≤ section length |
| **A4** | Switch clearing time includes switch re-setting time |
| **A5** | For conflicting switch routes, use the larger headway |
| **A6** | The big-M constant is chosen as $M \geq T^{max} + \max_{i,k,p} \beta_{i,k,p}$ |
| **A7** | All constraints are linear; no quadratic or nonlinear terms appear |
| **A8** | The model is solved in a rolling-horizon fashion for real-time application |

---

## 8. Remarks on Real-Time Applicability

1. **Rolling Horizon:** The model is re-solved periodically (e.g., every 30–60 seconds) with updated train positions and revised entry times $r_i^{entry}$.

2. **Warm Starts:** Previous solutions can be used as starting points to accelerate re-optimization.

3. **Preprocessing:** Pairs of trains that can never conflict (due to time separation) can be removed from $\mathcal{P}_s^{pair}$ to reduce model size.

4. **Profile Restriction:** In practice, $\mathcal{P}_i$ may be restricted to 2–3 profiles per section to limit combinatorial complexity.

5. **Reordering:** The binary sequencing variables $y_{(i,k),(j,l)}$ implicitly allow reordering (overtaking) at locations where the network topology permits (e.g., stations with multiple platforms, passing loops).

This model extends the RECIFE-MILP framework by explicitly incorporating **speed-dependent braking distances** under ETCS Level 2 DTG signalling, making the headway constraints train- and profile-dependent rather than fixed.

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of track sections (blocks/TDS), indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{S}^{SW} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Subset of switch sections |
| $\mathcal{S}^{PT} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Subset of plain track sections ($\mathcal{S}^{SW} \cup \mathcal{S}^{PT} = \mathcal{S}$, $\mathcal{S}^{SW} \cap \mathcal{S}^{PT} = \emptyset$) |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of discrete speed profiles available to train $i$, indexed by $p$ (e.g., $\{1=\text{full}, 2=\text{medium}, 3=\text{low}\}$) |
| $\mathcal{R}_i = (s_i^1, s_i^2, \ldots, s_i^{n_i})$ | Ordered route of train $i$: sequence of sections |
| $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$ | The $k$-th section on train $i$'s route, $k = 1, \ldots, n_i$ |
| $\mathcal{K}_i = \{1, \ldots, n_i\}$ | Position index set for train $i$'s route |
| $\mathcal{S}_i$ | Set of sections traversed by train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{C}_s = \{(i,j) : i, j \in \mathcal{T},\; i \neq j,\; s \in \mathcal{S}_i \cap \mathcal{S}_j\}$ | Set of train pairs potentially conflicting on section $s$ |
| $\mathcal{A}_i \subseteq \mathcal{K}_i$ | Set of route positions where train $i$ has a scheduled stop (station) |
| $\mathcal{D}_i \subseteq \mathcal{K}_i$ | Set of route positions where delay is measured (station arrivals, network exit) |
| $\mathcal{Q} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Set of sections where overtaking/reordering is permitted |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $r_i^{p}(s)$ | Running time of train $i$ on section $s$ under speed profile $p \in \mathcal{P}_i$ |
| $b_i^{p}(s)$ | Braking distance of train $i$ entering section $s$ under speed profile $p$ (train- and speed-dependent) |
| $v_i^{p}(s)$ | Entry speed of train $i$ on section $s$ under profile $p$ |
| $\tau_i^{p}(s)$ | Time for train $i$ to cover braking distance $b_i^{p}(s)$ at speed $v_i^{p}(s)$, i.e., $\tau_i^{p}(s) = b_i^{p}(s) / v_i^{p}(s)$ |
| $e_i$ | Earliest entry time of train $i$ into the network (release time) |
| $a_i^{sched}(k)$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at route position $k \in \mathcal{A}_i$ |
| $d_i^{sched}(k)$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from route position $k \in \mathcal{A}_i$ |
| $w_i^{min}(k)$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at route position $k \in \mathcal{A}_i$ |
| $L(s)$ | Length of section $s$ |
| $c_i(s)$ | Clearing time: time for train $i$ to fully clear section $s$ after its front reaches the section end (tail clearance) |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large positive constant (big-M) |
| $\omega_i(k)$ | Weight (priority) of delay for train $i$ at route position $k \in \mathcal{D}_i$ |
| $T^{hor}$ | Time horizon of the optimization |
| $\sigma_{ij}(s)$ | Minimum additional safety separation time between trains $i$ and $j$ on section $s$ (fixed safety margin) |

**Assumption 1.** The braking distance $b_i^p(s)$ depends on the train's braking curve (deceleration rate), the entry speed $v_i^p(s)$, and the gradient of section $s$. Under ETCS Level 2 DTG signalling, the movement authority extends to the end of the next section, so the follower must maintain a distance such that it can stop before the end of its authority.

**Assumption 2.** The time to cover the braking distance is approximated as $\tau_i^p(s) = b_i^p(s) / v_i^p(s)$, which is a conservative (constant-speed) approximation. This is a parameter computed offline for each $(i, p, s)$ combination.

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Continuous Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $t_i^{arr}(k)$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at the **beginning** of the section at route position $k \in \mathcal{K}_i$ |
| $t_i^{dep}(k)$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Departure time of train $i$ from the **beginning** of the section at route position $k \in \mathcal{K}_i$ (i.e., the time train $i$ starts traversing section $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$) |
| $t_i^{exit}(k)$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Time at which train $i$ fully **exits** (clears) section $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$ |
| $\delta_i(k)$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ | Delay of train $i$ at route position $k \in \mathcal{D}_i$ (positive deviation from schedule) |

### 3.2 Binary Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_i^{p}(k)$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $= 1$ if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on section $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$; $0$ otherwise |
| $y_{ij}(s)$ | $\{0,1\}$ | $= 1$ if train $i$ enters section $s$ **before** train $j$; $= 0$ if $j$ enters before $i$ (sequencing variable for $(i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s$) |

---

## 4. Auxiliary Expressions (Linear)

The **effective running time** of train $i$ on section $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$:

$$\rho_i(k) = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} r_i^{p}(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \cdot x_i^{p}(k)$$

The **effective braking time** of train $i$ entering section $\mathcal{R}_i(k)$:

$$\beta_i(k) = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} \tau_i^{p}(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \cdot x_i^{p}(k)$$

Both are linear in the binary profile selection variables.

---

## 5. Objective Function

$$\min \quad Z = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{D}_i} \omega_i(k) \cdot \delta_i(k)$$

**Explanation:** Minimize the total weighted delay across all trains at designated measurement points (station arrivals, network exits). The weights $\omega_i(k)$ encode train priorities (e.g., high-speed passenger trains may have higher weights than freight trains).

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Speed Profile Selection (Exactly One Profile per Train per Section)

$$\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} x_i^{p}(k) = 1 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{1}$$

**Explanation:** Each train must select exactly one speed profile for each section on its route. This links the binary profile variables to the running time and braking distance expressions.

---

### 6.2 Temporal Propagation Along the Route (Running Time Constraints)

$$t_i^{arr}(k+1) = t_i^{dep}(k) + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} r_i^{p}(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \cdot x_i^{p}(k) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i : k < n_i \tag{2}$$

**Explanation:** The arrival time at the start of the next section equals the departure time from the current section plus the running time on the current section, which depends on the selected speed profile. This is linear because $r_i^p$ is a parameter and $x_i^p$ is a binary variable.

---

### 6.3 Section Exit (Clearing) Time

$$t_i^{exit}(k) = t_i^{dep}(k) + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} r_i^{p}(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \cdot x_i^{p}(k) + c_i(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{3}$$

**Explanation:** The exit time from a section is the departure time plus the running time plus the clearing time $c_i(s)$ (time for the tail of the train to clear the section after the front reaches the end).

---

### 6.4 Release Time Constraints (No Early Start)

$$t_i^{dep}(1) \geq e_i \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T} \tag{4}$$

**Explanation:** Train $i$ cannot enter the network (depart from the start of its first section) before its release/entry time $e_i$.

---

### 6.5 Dwell Time Constraints at Scheduled Stops

$$t_i^{dep}(k) \geq t_i^{arr}(k) + w_i^{min}(k) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{A}_i \tag{5}$$

**Explanation:** At each scheduled stop, the train must dwell for at least the minimum dwell time $w_i^{min}(k)$ before departing.

---

### 6.6 Scheduled Departure Constraints (No Early Departure from Stops)

$$t_i^{dep}(k) \geq d_i^{sched}(k) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{A}_i \tag{6}$$

**Explanation:** A train cannot depart from a scheduled stop before its scheduled departure time. This enforces the timetable as a lower bound (retiming is allowed only as delays, not early departures).

**Assumption 3.** Early departures from stations are not permitted (standard in railway CDR). If early departures were allowed, this constraint would be relaxed.

---

### 6.7 Departure Equals Arrival at Non-Stop Sections

$$t_i^{dep}(k) = t_i^{arr}(k) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \setminus \mathcal{A}_i \tag{7}$$

**Explanation:** At sections where the train does not have a scheduled stop, the departure time equals the arrival time (no dwell).

---

### 6.8 Delay Definition Constraints

$$\delta_i(k) \geq t_i^{arr}(k) - a_i^{sched}(k) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{D}_i \tag{8}$$

$$\delta_i(k) \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{D}_i \tag{9}$$

**Explanation:** The delay $\delta_i(k)$ is the positive deviation of the actual arrival time from the scheduled arrival time. Since we minimize, $\delta_i(k)$ will take the value $\max(0, t_i^{arr}(k) - a_i^{sched}(k))$ at optimality.

---

### 6.9 Blocking Time / Separation Constraints under ETCS Level 2 DTG

For each section $s \in \mathcal{S}$ and each pair of trains $(i, j) \in \mathcal{C}_s$ sharing section $s$, let $k_i$ and $k_j$ be the route positions such that $\mathcal{R}_i(k_i) = s$ and $\mathcal{R}_j(k_j) = s$.

**Case A: Train $i$ leads, train $j$ follows** (enforced when $y_{ij}(s) = 1$):

$$t_j^{dep}(k_j) \geq t_i^{exit}(k_i) + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_j} \tau_j^{p}(s) \cdot x_j^{p}(k_j) + \sigma_{ij}(s) - M \cdot (1 - y_{ij}(s)) \tag{10a}$$

**Case B: Train $j$ leads, train $i$ follows** (enforced when $y_{ij}(s) = 0$):

$$t_i^{dep}(k_i) \geq t_j^{exit}(k_j) + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} \tau_i^{p}(s) \cdot x_i^{p}(k_i) + \sigma_{ji}(s) - M \cdot y_{ij}(s) \tag{10b}$$

**Explanation:** These are the core DTG blocking time constraints. Under ETCS Level 2 with distance-to-go signalling:

- When train $i$ leads ($y_{ij}(s) = 1$), constraint (10a) becomes active and (10b) is relaxed by the big-M term. The follower $j$ may enter section $s$ only after:
  1. The leader $i$ has fully cleared section $s$ (i.e., $t_i^{exit}(k_i)$), **plus**
  2. The time $\tau_j^p(s) = b_j^p(s)/v_j^p(s)$ needed for the follower $j$ to cover its speed-dependent braking distance (so that $j$'s braking curve does not violate the end of authority at the section end), **plus**
  3. A fixed safety margin $\sigma_{ij}(s)$.

- When train $j$ leads ($y_{ij}(s) = 0$), constraint (10b) becomes active instead, with the roles reversed.

- The binary variable $y_{ij}(s)$ determines the **sequencing** (order) of trains on section $s$. The big-M formulation creates a disjunctive constraint: exactly one of the two cases is enforced.

**Assumption 4.** The braking distance $b_j^p(s)$ is computed based on the entry speed $v_j^p(s)$ associated with the selected profile $p$, the train's deceleration capability, and the section gradient. Under DTG, the movement authority for the follower extends to the end of the section occupied by the leader, so the follower must be able to stop within that distance.

**Assumption 5.** For switch sections $s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW}$, an additional constraint may be needed to account for route setting and locking time. This is captured by a potentially larger $\sigma_{ij}(s)$ for switch sections.

---

### 6.10 Switch Section Route Compatibility (Optional but Recommended)

For switch sections $s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW}$, if trains $i$ and $j$ require **conflicting switch positions** (different routes through the switch), an additional switch re-setting time $\Delta^{SW}(s)$ is required:

$$t_j^{dep}(k_j) \geq t_i^{exit}(k_i) + \Delta^{SW}(s) - M \cdot (1 - y_{ij}(s)) \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s^{conflict},\; s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW} \tag{11a}$$

$$t_i^{dep}(k_i) \geq t_j^{exit}(k_j) + \Delta^{SW}(s) - M \cdot y_{ij}(s) \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s^{conflict},\; s \in \mathcal{S}^{SW} \tag{11b}$$

where $\mathcal{C}_s^{conflict} \subseteq \mathcal{C}_s$ is the set of train pairs requiring different switch positions on section $s$.

**Explanation:** When two consecutive trains need different switch alignments, additional time is needed for the switch to be re-positioned and locked. This is added on top of the normal separation.

---

### 6.11 Reordering Constraints (Optional — at Designated Locations)

For sections $s \in \mathcal{Q}$ (where reordering is permitted), the sequencing variables $y_{ij}(s)$ are **free binary variables** — the optimizer decides the order.

For sections $s \notin \mathcal{Q}$ (where reordering is **not** permitted), the order is fixed according to the original timetable or current state:

$$y_{ij}(s) = 1 \quad \forall (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s,\; s \notin \mathcal{Q},\; \text{if } i \text{ is scheduled before } j \text{ on } s \tag{12}$$

**Explanation:** At suitable locations (e.g., stations with multiple platforms, passing loops), the optimizer can choose to reorder trains. Elsewhere, the order is fixed to maintain feasibility and safety.

**Assumption 6.** Reordering is only allowed at sections in $\mathcal{Q}$. This is a modeling choice; in practice, $\mathcal{Q}$ typically includes station areas and dedicated overtaking points.

---

### 6.12 Retiming Constraints (Optional)

If retiming (adjusting scheduled times within limits) is permitted, introduce slack variables:

$$t_i^{dep}(k) \geq d_i^{sched}(k) - \epsilon_i^{dep}(k) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{A}_i \tag{13}$$

$$\epsilon_i^{dep}(k) \leq \bar{\epsilon} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{A}_i \tag{14}$$

where $\epsilon_i^{dep}(k) \geq 0$ is the allowed departure time adjustment and $\bar{\epsilon}$ is the maximum allowed retiming. A penalty term $\sum_{i,k} \gamma_i(k) \cdot \epsilon_i^{dep}(k)$ can be added to the objective.

**Assumption 7.** If retiming is not allowed, set $\bar{\epsilon} = 0$, which recovers constraint (6).

---

### 6.13 Time Horizon Constraints

$$t_i^{arr}(k) \leq T^{hor} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{15}$$

$$t_i^{dep}(k) \leq T^{hor} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{16}$$

**Explanation:** All event times must lie within the optimization time horizon.

---

### 6.14 Variable Domain Constraints

$$t_i^{arr}(k), \; t_i^{dep}(k), \; t_i^{exit}(k) \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{17}$$

$$\delta_i(k) \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{D}_i \tag{18}$$

$$x_i^{p}(k) \in \{0, 1\} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T},\; k \in \mathcal{K}_i,\; p \in \mathcal{P}_i \tag{19}$$

$$y_{ij}(s) \in \{0, 1\} \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{S},\; (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s \tag{20}$$

---

## 7. Complete Model Summary

$$\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{D}_i} \omega_i(k) \cdot \delta_i(k) \\[6pt]
\text{s.t.} \quad
& \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} x_i^{p}(k) = 1 && \forall i, k \\
& t_i^{arr}(k+1) = t_i^{dep}(k) + \sum_{p} r_i^{p}(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \cdot x_i^{p}(k) && \forall i, k < n_i \\
& t_i^{exit}(k) = t_i^{dep}(k) + \sum_{p} r_i^{p}(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) \cdot x_i^{p}(k) + c_i(\mathcal{R}_i(k)) && \forall i, k \\
& t_i^{dep}(1) \geq e_i && \forall i \\
& t_i^{dep}(k) \geq t_i^{arr}(k) + w_i^{min}(k) && \forall i, k \in \mathcal{A}_i \\
& t_i^{dep}(k) \geq d_i^{sched}(k) && \forall i, k \in \mathcal{A}_i \\
& t_i^{dep}(k) = t_i^{arr}(k) && \forall i, k \notin \mathcal{A}_i \\
& \delta_i(k) \geq t_i^{arr}(k) - a_i^{sched}(k) && \forall i, k \in \mathcal{D}_i \\
& t_j^{dep}(k_j) \geq t_i^{exit}(k_i) + \sum_{p} \tau_j^{p}(s) \cdot x_j^{p}(k_j) + \sigma_{ij}(s) - M(1 - y_{ij}(s)) && \forall s, (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s \\
& t_i^{dep}(k_i) \geq t_j^{exit}(k_j) + \sum_{p} \tau_i^{p}(s) \cdot x_i^{p}(k_i) + \sigma_{ji}(s) - M \cdot y_{ij}(s)) && \forall s, (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s \\
& y_{ij}(s) = 1 && \forall s \notin \mathcal{Q}, (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s, \; i \prec j \\
& t_i^{arr}(k), t_i^{dep}(k), t_i^{exit}(k) \in [0, T^{hor}] && \forall i, k \\
& \delta_i(k) \geq 0 && \forall i, k \in \mathcal{D}_i \\
& x_i^{p}(k) \in \{0,1\} && \forall i, k, p \\
& y_{ij}(s) \in \{0,1\} && \forall s, (i,j) \in \mathcal{C}_s
\end{aligned}$$

---

## 8. Explanation of Model Elements

### 8.1 Microscopic Network Representation
The network is modeled at the **microscopic level** as a set of track sections (blocks or Track Detection Sections, TDS). Each section is either a **switch section** (containing points/turnouts) or a **plain track section**. This distinction matters because switch sections require additional route-setting time and may have different speed restrictions.

### 8.2 Speed Profile Selection
Each train can choose from a finite set of speed profiles on each section. The profile determines:
- **Running time** $r_i^p(s)$: lower speed → longer running time
- **Braking distance** $b_i^p(s)$: lower entry speed → shorter braking distance → smaller required headway

This creates a trade-off: a slower profile increases the train's own running time but may reduce the required separation from the leader, potentially reducing overall delay in congested situations.

### 8.3 DTG Blocking Time Logic
Under ETCS Level 2 with distance-to-go signalling:
- The **movement authority (MA)** for a train extends to the end of the section ahead (or beyond, depending on the radio block center's grant).
- The **follower** must maintain sufficient distance so that its **braking curve** (from its current speed to a stop) does not exceed the end of its MA.
- The constraint (10a)/(10b) ensures: the follower enters section $s$ only after the leader has cleared it **plus** the time the follower needs to cover its braking distance. This is the **speed-dependent headway**.

### 8.4 Big-M Disjunctive Formulation
For each pair of trains sharing a section, exactly one of two orderings is possible:
- $y_{ij}(s) = 1$: train $i$ goes first → constraint (10a) is active, (10b) is relaxed
- $y_{ij}(s) = 0$: train $j$ goes first → constraint (10b) is active, (10a) is relaxed

The big-M constant must be chosen large enough to relax the inactive constraint but not so large as to cause numerical issues. A safe choice is $M = T^{hor} + \max_{i,p,s} \tau_i^p(s) + \max_{i,j,s} \sigma_{ij}(s)$.

### 8.5 Conflict Detection and Resolution
- **Detection**: Conflicts arise when the separation constraints (10a)/(10b) would be violated under the current timetable/ordering.
- **Resolution**: The optimizer resolves conflicts by:
  1. **Reordering**: choosing optimal values for $y_{ij}(s)$ at locations where reordering is allowed
  2. **Retiming**: adjusting departure/arrival times within timetable constraints
  3. **Speed profile adjustment**: selecting slower profiles to reduce braking distances and required headways

### 8.6 Linearity
All constraints are linear in the decision variables:
- Running times and braking times are **linear combinations** of binary profile variables with constant coefficients.
- The disjunctive constraints use the standard **big-M** technique, which is linear.
- Delay definitions use **linear inequalities** (the max function is captured by the minimization objective).
- No products of variables appear anywhere in the model.

---

## 9. Assumptions Summary

| # | Assumption |
|---|-----------|
| 1 | Braking distances are precomputed parameters based on train characteristics, entry speed, and section gradient. |
| 2 | Braking time $\tau_i^p(s) = b_i^p(s)/v_i^p(s)$ is a conservative constant-speed approximation. |
| 3 | Early departures from scheduled stops are not permitted. |
| 4 | Under DTG, the movement authority extends to the end of the next section; the follower must stop within this distance. |
| 5 | Switch sections may require additional route-setting time $\Delta^{SW}(s)$. |
| 6 | Reordering is only allowed at designated sections $\mathcal{Q}$. |
| 7 | Retiming is optional and bounded by $\bar{\epsilon}$. |
| 8 | Each train follows a fixed route (no rerouting); only reordering, retiming, and speed profile changes are allowed. |
| 9 | The clearing time $c_i(s)$ accounts for the train length and is a fixed parameter. |
| 10 | The model is solved in a rolling-horizon fashion for real-time application, with $e_i$ updated to reflect the current state. |
